fort genois de tabarka.d: A 16th-century Genoese fortress overlooking the old port of Tabarka, a remnant of the Lomellini family’s presence. A lighthouse was added in the late 19th century.

fort santiago (borj chikly).a: The Hispano-Ottoman fort on the islet of Chikly in the middle of the lake, rebuilt in the 16th century on older foundations, within the bird sanctuary.
fort santiago (borj chikly).c: Access to the islet is restricted (permit required, boat crossing): please check with the INP before visiting.
fort santiago (borj chikly).d: A fort stands on the islet of Chikly, in the middle of Lake Tunis. A former citadel of Roman origin, rebuilt by the Spanish governor of La Goulette between 1546 and 1550 (Santiago de Chikly). Listed as a national cultural heritage site in 1993.

foussana.a: A town in the north-west of Kasserine, between Djebel Bireno and the Algerian border.
foussana.c: A stop-off on the way to Djebel Bireno; check access to this mountainous border area.
foussana.d: A town in the north-west of the Kasserine governorate, near the Algerian border.

gaafour.a: A stopover town on the north-western railway line.
gaafour.c: Primarily a transport hub; of little tourist interest in its own right.
gaafour.d: A town in the governorate of Siliana, on the north-western railway line.

garaa sejnane.a: The wetland and marsh near Sejnane, important for migratory birds.
garaa sejnane.c: Visit during the wet season for waterbirds; binoculars recommended, to be combined with a visit to the town of Sejnane.
garaa sejnane.d: North-western wetland (marsh) near Sejnane, important for migratory birdlife.

ghannouch.a: A municipality on the Gulf of Gabès, to the north of the city.
ghannouch.c: Ordinary town: of limited interest to visitors; more of a stopover.
ghannouch.d: Municipality and administrative centre of the Gabès governorate, on the Gulf to the north of the city.

ghomrassen.a: A former Berber settlement in a valley of cliffs dotted with cave granaries.
ghomrassen.c: A convenient starting point for exploring the surrounding ksour; bring water.
ghomrassen.d: A town in the south-east, about 26 km from Tataouine, a former Berber settlement in a valley of cliffs and cave granaries.

gightis (gigthis).a: Remains of a Punic and later Roman city on the Gulf of Bou Ghrara: paved forum, capitol, thermal baths and temple foundations.
gightis (gigthis).c: Site open during the day, with little shade: bring water and a hat, and check the AMVPPC’s opening times on site.
gightis (gigthis).d: Former Punic trading post and later a Roman city on the Gulf of Bou Ghrara, featuring a forum, capitol, thermal baths and temples.
gightis (gigthis).h: Site managed by the AMVPPC — open during the day; opening hours vary according to the season, so please check on site.

gisement prehistorique d'el mekta (capsi.a: The eponymous site of the Capsian culture: snail shell mounds and stone tool production from the Epipalaeolithic period.
gisement prehistorique d'el mekta (capsi.c: A site of mainly scientific interest, not particularly spectacular: a guide or the Gafsa museum will help you understand it.
gisement prehistorique d'el mekta (capsi.d: The eponymous site and key reference point for Capsian culture (Epipalaeolithic) near Gafsa, featuring snail shell mounds and stone tool production. Coordinates of the site.

golfe de gabes (petite syrte).a: A large gulf on the south-east coast, the ancient Petite Syrte, notable for its significant tidal range.
golfe de gabes (petite syrte).c: The tidal range exposes much of the foreshore: check the tide times for the seaside.
golfe de gabes (petite syrte).d: A large gulf on the south-east coast opening onto the Mediterranean, formerly known as Petite Syrte, with a significant tidal range.

gorges de selja.a: The steep-sided valley of the Selja wadi between Metlaoui and Redeyef, a nature reserve through which the Lezard Rouge railway runs.
gorges de selja.c: The train is the best way to explore the gorges; book in advance during peak season.
gorges de selja.d: A steep-sided valley several km long through which the Selja wadi flows, between Metlaoui and Redeyef (Gafsa). A nature reserve (675 ha) since 2009, crossed by the Red Lizard.

grand chapiteau corinthien (el jem).a: Large ancient Corinthian capital amongst the scattered ruins of Thysdrus in El Jem.
grand chapiteau corinthien (el jem).c: A detail to look out for when visiting the Roman ruins at El Jem.
grand chapiteau corinthien (el jem).d: A large ancient Corinthian capital amongst the Roman ruins of Thysdrus in El Jem.

grand erg oriental.a: A vast sea of Saharan dunes stretching as far as south-western Tunisia (Douz, Ksar Ghilane).
grand erg oriental.c: A 4x4, guide and water are essential; the dunes are stunning at sunrise and sunset.
grand erg oriental.d: A vast sea of Saharan dunes stretching across Algeria and south-western Tunisia (the Douz and Ksar Ghilane region). A spot located in Ksar Ghilane, the Tunisian gateway to the erg.

grande mosquee de beja.a: The main mosque of the medina of Béja, founded in 944 on the site of an ancient basilica and restored in 1922.
grande mosquee de beja.c: Appropriate attire required; well worth a visit whilst strolling through the medina of Béja.
grande mosquee de beja.d: The main mosque of the medina of Beja, founded in 944 on the site of an ancient basilica and restored in 1922.

grande mosquee de gafsa.a: The Great Mosque in the heart of the Gafsa oasis, a stone’s throw from the Roman baths.
grande mosquee de gafsa.c: The interior is often reserved for worshippers; combine your visit with a trip to the nearby medina.
grande mosquee de gafsa.d: The Great Mosque of Gafsa in the heart of the oasis, close to the town’s Roman baths. Region of prehistoric Capsian culture.

grande mosquee de kairouan.a: the vast courtyard and its sundial; the massive three-storey minaret; the prayer hall with its reused columns and mihrab adorned with lustre tiles.
grande mosquee de kairouan.c: Appropriate attire is required; the courtyard is open to visitors, whilst the prayer hall can be viewed from the threshold.
grande mosquee de kairouan.d: The Great Mosque of Kairouan (Oqba ibn Nafi Mosque), one of the oldest and most important religious complexes in the Muslim West, founded in the 7th century.
grande mosquee de kairouan.h: Place of worship — visits possible during opening hours; appropriate attire required.

grande mosquee de mahdia.a: the monumental portico façade and its projecting gateway, a reconstruction of the 10th-century Fatimid plan; the courtyard opening out onto the sea.
grande mosquee de mahdia.c: Beautiful late-afternoon light on the light-coloured stone, facing the harbour.
grande mosquee de mahdia.d: The Great Fatimid Mosque of Mahdia, rebuilt identically in the 20th century based on its original 10th-century plans.
grande mosquee de mahdia.h: Place of worship — visits possible during opening hours; appropriate dress required.

grande mosquee de monastir.a: A mosque of medieval origin that has been remodelled several times, situated right next to the ribat.
grande mosquee de monastir.c: Best visited in conjunction with the nearby ribat; appropriate attire required.
grande mosquee de monastir.d: The Great Mosque of Monastir, adjacent to the ribat, dates from the Middle Ages and has been remodelled several times.
grande mosquee de monastir.h: Place of worship — visits possible during opening hours; appropriate attire required.

grande mosquee de nabeul.a: The Great Mosque of Nabeul, listed as a historic monument since 1915.
grande mosquee de nabeul.c: Well worth a visit whilst strolling through the medina of Nabeul; modest dress is required.
grande mosquee de nabeul.d: The Great Mosque of Nabeul, listed as a historic monument since 3 March 1915.

grande mosquee de sfax.a: The minaret with its carved geometric decoration; the façades adorned with inscriptions; its location at the heart of the medina’s souks.
grande mosquee de sfax.c: Walk around the minaret through the narrow streets of the souks to take in the decorations.
grande mosquee de sfax.d: The Great Mosque in the heart of the Sfax medina, founded during the Aghlabid period (9th century) and enlarged on several occasions.
grande mosquee de sfax.h: Place of worship — visits possible during opening hours; appropriate attire required.

grande mosquee de sousse.a: the courtyard lined with galleries; the corner turrets reminiscent of a fortress; the simple Aghlabid prayer hall.
grande mosquee de sousse.c: Just a stone’s throw from the ribat, well worth including in the same tour of the medina.
grande mosquee de sousse.d: The 9th-century Great Mosque of Sousse, with its simple, fortified layout, is situated in the heart of the medina near the ribat.
grande mosquee de sousse.h: Place of worship — visits possible during opening hours; appropriate dress required.

grande mosquee de testour.a: the Hispano-Moorish minaret with a clock; the Andalusian décor brought by the Moriscos; the town square of the town founded in the 17th century.
grande mosquee de testour.c: Combine with the Malouf festival in summer; picturesque Andalusian village on the Medjerda.
grande mosquee de testour.d: Testour Mosque, in a town founded in the 17th century by Andalusians (Moriscos) expelled from Spain; minaret with Hispano-Moorish influences, featuring a clock.
grande mosquee de testour.h: Place of worship — visits possible during opening hours; appropriate dress required.

grande mosquee de zaghouan.a: The Hanafi mosque and its minaret in the old town, at the foot of the djebel.
grande mosquee de zaghouan.c: Well worth seeing whilst strolling through the medina of Zaghouan and its fountains.
grande mosquee de zaghouan.d: The Hanafi mosque in the town of Zaghouan, set within the historic town centre at the foot of the djebel.

grande synagogue de tunis.a: The Art Deco façade of the capital’s main synagogue, built in the modern part of the city in the late 1930s, on Avenue de la Liberté.
grande synagogue de tunis.c: Access is restricted and secured: please enquire in advance if you wish to visit.
grande synagogue de tunis.d: Tunis’s main synagogue, built in the late 1930s in the modern part of the city in the Art Deco style.

grotte des chauves-souris (el haouaria).a: A cave harbouring bats, near El Haouaria at the tip of Cap Bon.
grotte des chauves-souris (el haouaria).c: Best visited in combination with the nearby Roman quarries; a torch and suitable footwear are recommended.
grotte des chauves-souris (el haouaria).d: Bat cave near El Haouaria, at the tip of Cap Bon.

guellala (djerba).a: A village in southern Djerba, a historic centre for pottery, with workshops and cave kilns.
guellala (djerba).c: Visit a potter’s workshop; the shops are concentrated along the main road.
guellala (djerba).d: A village in southern Djerba, a historic centre for pottery thanks to its clay deposits. A pottery tradition dating back to antiquity, with workshops and cave kilns.

guermessa (ksar et village).a: A hilltop Berber village with a hilltop ksar, quieter and less crowded than Chenini and Douiret.
guermessa (ksar et village).c: Access can be tricky at times: a 4x4 or a local guide makes the climb easier.
guermessa (ksar et village).d: A hilltop Berber village with a ksar on the ridge, in the Tataouine region, less crowded than Chenini and Douiret.

hadrumete (hadrumetum, sousse antique).a: Layers of ancient Hadrumetum beneath modern-day Sousse: a Punic and then Roman heritage, which gave rise to the Christian catacombs and the mosaics on display in the museum.
hadrumete (hadrumetum, sousse antique).c: As the remains are scattered beneath the modern city, the Kasbah Archaeological Museum offers the best overview.
hadrumete (hadrumetum, sousse antique).d: An ancient Phoenician settlement that became a major Roman city (Hadrumetum), beneath present-day Sousse. Christian catacombs and rich mosaics.

hafsia.a: The second-hand clothes market; the restored architecture blending the old with the rebuilt; the legacy of the Jewish quarter.
hafsia.c: A place to hunt for bargains and get a feel for today’s working-class Tunis. Haggling is a must.
hafsia.d: The former Jewish quarter of the medina (the ‘hara’), where Jews were welcomed as early as the 10th century by Sidi Mahrez. Having fallen into poverty and then been partially demolished, it was restored in the 1970s and 1980s by the Association for the Preservation of the Medina — an award-winning project that has become a textbook example of urban planning. Today, it is home to the famous second-hand clothes market.

haidra (ammaedara).a: The vast Byzantine fortress with its imposing ramparts, triumphal arches, the Church of Melleus and several Christian basilicas near the Algerian border.
haidra (ammaedara).c: A sprawling and remote site: bring plenty of water, allow two hours for your visit, and check the access details before setting off.
haidra (ammaedara).d: An ancient Roman and later Byzantine city near the Algerian border, featuring a vast Byzantine fortress, arches and Christian basilicas.
haidra (ammaedara).h: Site managed by the AMVPPC — open during the day; opening hours vary by season, so check on site.

hammam bourguiba.a: The thermal spring nestled in the Kroumirie forest, near the Algerian border.
hammam bourguiba.c: A relaxing stop after forest walks; best combined with a visit to nearby Ain Draham.
hammam bourguiba.d: A thermal spring in the Kroumirie forest area, near the Algerian border. Coordinates centred on the locality.

hammam lif.a: The seafront and the casino – a former Beylical holiday resort at the foot of Boukornine – the thermal springs and the resort’s old-fashioned seaside atmosphere.
hammam lif.c: Starting point for the climb to Boukornine National Park, which overlooks the town.
hammam lif.d: A seaside and spa resort at the foot of Djebel Boukornine, on the Gulf of Tunis. A former Beylical holiday resort with hot springs.

hammam mellegue (thermes romains).a: Roman baths still fed by thermal waters, with ancient pools and structures still in use, on the banks of the Mellegue wadi.
hammam mellegue (thermes romains).c: Access is via a track about ten km south-west of El Kef: ensure you have a suitable vehicle and check the road conditions.
hammam mellegue (thermes romains).d: Ancient Roman thermal baths still in use, on the Mellegue wadi about ten kilometres south-west of Le Kef. Original pools and structures still fed by thermal waters.

haras national de sidi thabet.a: The historic horse breeding centre specialising in Barb and Arab-Barb horses, its stables and its thoroughbreds.
haras national de sidi thabet.c: Of interest to horse enthusiasts; check the visiting conditions and opening hours.
haras national de sidi thabet.d: The historic Sidi Thabet horse breeding centre (Barb and Arab-Barb horses).

hassi el ferid.a: A small sub-prefecture town in the south-west of Kasserine, with no major sites.
hassi el ferid.d: A town and sub-prefecture in the south-west of the Kasserine governorate.

hazoua.a: A small oasis town near the Algerian border, in the governorate of Tozeur.
hazoua.c: Remote border town: make sure you have enough water and fuel.
hazoua.d: A small oasis town in the governorate of Tozeur, close to the Algerian border.

henchir bou zer.a: Ancient ruins (henchir) in the north of the Sidi Bouzid governorate; rather unspectacular remains.
henchir bou zer.d: Ruins (Henchir) in the north of the governorate of Sidi Bouzid.

henchir-bez.a: Ancient archaeological site (henchir) in the north-west of the Kairouan governorate; modest remains.
henchir-bez.c: Of mainly archaeological interest: check locally for access details.
henchir-bez.d: Ancient archaeological site (henchir) in the north-west of the Kairouan governorate.

henchir-bir-el-menadla.a: Ancient archaeological site (henchir) in the west of the Mahdia governorate; modest remains.
henchir-bir-el-menadla.c: Mainly of archaeological interest: check locally for access details.
henchir-bir-el-menadla.d: Ancient archaeological site (henchir) to the west of the Mahdia governorate, near the border with Kairouan.

henchir-khachoum (muzuca).a: The scattered remains of ancient Muzuca, a Roman civitas and former seat of a bishopric.
henchir-khachoum (muzuca).c: A modest, largely undeveloped rural site: of particular interest to archaeology enthusiasts with precise coordinates.
henchir-khachoum (muzuca).d: A group of sites in the governorate of Sidi Bouzid, identified as the ancient Muzuca, a Roman civitas and the seat of a bishopric attached to Carthage.

hergla (horrea caelia).a: The white village perched on the cliff; the Sidi Bou Mendil Mosque; the narrow streets overlooking the sea and the old mat-weaving workshop.
hergla (horrea caelia).c: A picturesque stop-off between Sousse and Hammamet; beautiful views out to sea from the edge of the plateau.
hergla (horrea caelia).d: A small white coastal town in the Gulf of Hammamet, on the site of the Roman town of Horrea Caelia. Medina featuring the Sidi Bou Mendil Mosque.

hotel sidi driss (decor star wars, ferme.a: A cave hotel in Matmata, whose courtyard served as the interior of the Lars’ farm in Star Wars (1977, then 2002 and 2005).
hotel sidi driss (decor star wars, ferme.c: The site is still in use: visitors can enjoy a cup of tea or stay overnight to see the set; it gets busy at peak times.
hotel sidi driss (decor star wars, ferme.d: The cave hotel in Matmata, whose inner courtyard served as the setting for the interior of the Lars’ farm (Luke Skywalker’s home) in Star Wars IV: A New Hope (1977), and was reused for Episodes II (2002) and III (2005). Distinct from the centre of Matmata.

houmt souk (djerba).a: The capital of Djerba: medina, traditional souks and old fondouks.
houmt souk (djerba).c: Stroll through the souks in the morning or evening, when the heat has subsided.
houmt souk (djerba).d: The main town and capital of Djerba, situated on the site of an ancient city. It features a medina, traditional souks and old fondouks.

ile conigliera.a: A small island off the Gulf of Monastir, part of the Kuriat archipelago.
ile conigliera.c: It can only be reached by sea, as part of an excursion to the Kuriat Islands.
ile conigliera.d: A small island off the coast of the Gulf of Monastir, part of the Kuriat archipelago.

ile de djerba.a: Tunisia’s largest island, a maritime oasis with lagoons, linked to the mainland by an ancient causeway.
ile de djerba.c: Hire a bike or a car to explore the island; the beaches and villages are well worth a visit.
ile de djerba.d: Tunisia’s largest island, in the Gulf of Gabès, connected to the mainland by an ancient causeway. A maritime oasis with lagoons.

ile de la galite (ile principale).a: The largest island in the volcanic La Galite archipelago, a nature reserve rich in birdlife and flora.
ile de la galite (ile principale).c: Access by boat during the summer months only; book an organised excursion and check the weather forecast.
ile de la galite (ile principale).d: The largest island in the volcanic La Galite archipelago, a nature reserve rich in birdlife and flora.

ile de zembra.a: The island’s cliffs and terrain; its rich marine life and bird colonies; the setting of the national park off Cap Bon.
ile de zembra.c: A protected reserve with restricted access: best reached by boat trip.
ile de zembra.d: A mountainous island off the coast of Cap Bon, at the heart of the Zembra and Zembretta Islands National Park and a UNESCO Biosphere Reserve.

ile pilau.a: The small island off the coast of Raf Raf and Cape Sidi Ali el-Mekki, with a distinctive silhouette facing the beach.
ile pilau.c: Best viewed from Raf Raf beach; there are no visitor facilities on the island.
ile pilau.d: A small island off the coast of Raf Raf and Cape Sidi Ali el-Mekki.

ile plane.a: The low-lying island topped by a lighthouse, off Cape Sidi Ali el-Mekki.
ile plane.c: Visible from the coast; well worth including in a tour of Ghar el Melh Bay.
ile plane.d: A low-lying island off Cape Sidi Ali el-Mekki, topped by a lighthouse.

ile zembretta.a: Small islet (~2 ha) to the east of Zembra, forming, together with it, a key area for the conservation of seabirds.
ile zembretta.c: Protected islet with restricted access; observation from the sea only.
ile zembretta.d: Small islet in the Gulf of Tunis, ~8 km east of Zembra (~2 ha). Together with Zembra, it forms an important area for the conservation of seabirds.

iles cani.a: The small rocky archipelago topped by a lighthouse, off the north coast of Bizerte, a nesting site for seabirds.
iles cani.c: Accessible only by boat and weather permitting; best visited as part of an organised boat trip.
iles cani.d: A small rocky archipelago off the northern coast of Bizerte, topped by a lighthouse. A nesting site for seabirds.

iles fratelli.a: The small rocky archipelago off the north-west coast, between Cape Serrat and Cape Negro.
iles fratelli.c: A navigational mark visible from the Kroumirie coastline; no landing permitted.
iles fratelli.d: A small rocky archipelago off the north-west coast, between Cape Serrat and Cape Negro.

iles kerkennah.a: Traditional ‘charfia’ fishing; the ports of Sidi Youssef and Sidi Frej; the low-lying beaches and palm groves; the Bordj El Hassar.
iles kerkennah.c: A slow-paced, timeless atmosphere; hire a bike and sample the local grilled octopus.
iles kerkennah.d: A low-lying, sandy archipelago off the coast of Sfax, surrounded by shoals and wetlands. Traditional fishing using the ‘charfia’ method.

iles kneiss.a: Archipelago and Ramsar nature reserve in the Gulf of Gabès, important for migratory birds.
iles kneiss.c: Protected area: access by sea; arrangements to be made locally whilst respecting the birdlife.
iles kneiss.d: Archipelago and nature reserve (Ramsar) in the Gulf of Gabès, important for migratory birds.

iles kuriat.a: White sandy beaches and crystal-clear waters; the old lighthouse; the loggerhead turtle nesting site.
iles kuriat.c: A day trip from Monastir in season; take shade and water with you, as the island has no facilities.
iles kuriat.d: A small archipelago off the coast of Monastir, a nesting site for loggerhead sea turtles and a marine protected area.

ilot de chikly.a: The small bird sanctuary in the middle of the lake and the Hispano-Ottoman fort of Santiago which overlooks it.
ilot de chikly.c: Access is restricted and requires authorisation from the INP, with a boat crossing: this must be arranged in advance.
ilot de chikly.d: A small islet in the middle of Lake Tunis, a nature reserve for birds and the site of a Hispano-Ottoman fort (Santiago).

jedelienne.a: A town in the north-east of Kasserine.
jedelienne.d: A town and sub-prefecture in the north-east of the governorate of Kasserine.

jemna.a: An oasis town in the Nefzaoua region, renowned for its springs and dates, with an old mosque housing an ancient library.
jemna.c: A stroll through the palm grove; intense heat in summer.
jemna.d: An oasis town in the Nefzaoua region, renowned for its springs and date production; it features an old mosque housing an ancient library.

jerissa.a: A mining town (iron) surrounded by Amazigh, Punic and Roman ruins.
jerissa.c: A stop for those interested in mining heritage and the ruins scattered around the area.
jerissa.d: A town in the Kef governorate, known for its iron mine and the Amazigh, Punic and Roman ruins in the surrounding area.

kalaa kebira.a: A city whose name means ‘great fortress’, centred around the old town ‘El Ksar’, founded under the Aghlabids and once surrounded by a rampart.
kalaa kebira.c: A nearby stopover from Sousse for those interested in the ancient fabric of the Sahel.
kalaa kebira.d: A town whose name means ‘great fortress’. The old town centre, ‘El Ksar’, was founded under the Aghlabids and was once surrounded by a rampart.

kalaat el-andalous.a: The Morisco village perched on its promontory, with its ancient alleyways and panoramic views of the lower Medjerda and the Ghar El Melh lagoon.
kalaat el-andalous.c: A beautiful viewpoint in the morning or evening light; well worth combining with a visit to the nearby mouth of the Medjerda.
kalaat el-andalous.d: A village founded by the Andalusians (Moriscos) in the 17th century, on a promontory overlooking the lower Medjerda and Lake Ghar El Melh.

kalaat es senam.a: A town at the foot of the spectacular Table de Jugurtha, the starting point for the ascent.
kalaat es senam.c: An ideal base before climbing the Table de Jugurtha: set off in the morning and take plenty of water with you.
kalaat es senam.d: A town in the west of the Kef governorate, at the foot of the Table de Jugurtha.

kasbah de beja.a: The citadel overlooking Béja, whose ramparts blend Punic, Byzantine and Ottoman features; today a cultural centre offering views over the town.
kasbah de beja.c: Accessible via a climb from the medina; best combined with a visit to the Great Mosque and the old town of Béja.
kasbah de beja.d: A citadel overlooking Beja, remodelled from Punic and Byzantine times through to the Ottoman period. A cultural centre since independence.

kasbah de bizerte.a: The fortress with its mighty ramparts guarding the entrance to the old harbour, with its inner alleyways and views over the channel.
kasbah de bizerte.c: Accessible on foot from the old harbour; wear sturdy shoes for the ramparts and narrow alleyways.
kasbah de bizerte.d: A fortress overlooking the entrance to the old port of Bizerte, with its imposing ramparts, protecting the town and its channel.

kasbah de hammamet.a: The fort overlooking the old town; the panoramic walkway offering views of the white medina and the beach; the flower-filled alleyways below.
kasbah de hammamet.c: Take a walk along the ramparts at sunset for views of the bay.
kasbah de hammamet.d: A fortress at the south-western corner of Hammamet’s medina, overlooking the sea. A 9th-century ribat used for coastal surveillance, rebuilt in the 15th century under the Hafsids.

kasbah de sfax.a: Fortress at the south-western corner of the medina, incorporated into the ramparts; it now houses a museum.
kasbah de sfax.c: Climb the ramparts for a panoramic view of the medina.
kasbah de sfax.d: Fortress at the south-western corner of the Sfax medina, integrated into the ramparts, commanding the defence of this sector. Approximate coordinates.

kasbah de sousse (tour du khalef).a: A fortress at the highest point of the medina, incorporating the Khalef Tower (859) and housing the archaeological museum, which boasts a rich collection of mosaics.
kasbah de sousse (tour du khalef).c: Combine a visit to the kasbah and its museum; the high point offers a fine view of the medina.
kasbah de sousse (tour du khalef).d: Fortress at the highest point of the medina of Sousse, incorporated into the ramparts in the 11th century, encompassing the Khalef Tower (859). Home to the archaeological museum.

kasbah du kef.a: The Ottoman fortress (from 1600) overlooking the medina, with its ramparts and bastions, is now a venue for cultural events.
kasbah du kef.c: Head up there in the late afternoon for panoramic views of the town and the plain; allow about an hour.
kasbah du kef.d: The Ottoman fortress of El Kef, built from 1600 onwards for the defence and administration of the city. It overlooks the medina and now hosts cultural events.

kasr-erressass (acholla).a: Listed monument at the ancient site of Acholla, on the Sahel coast.
kasr-erressass (acholla).c: To be included in a visit to the Acholla site.
kasr-erressass (acholla).d: Listed monument at the ancient site of Acholla.

kasserine (ville).a: The capital at the foot of Djebel Chambi, built on the site of ancient Cillium and the gateway to the national park.
kasserine (ville).c: A base for exploring Djebel Chambi and the sites of Cillium and the Mausoleum of the Flavii.
kasserine (ville).d: Capital of the governorate of Kasserine, at the foot of Djebel Chambi, on the site of ancient Cillium.

kebili.a: Capital of the Nefzaoua region, one of the oldest oases in North Africa, near the Chott el-Jerid, renowned for its Deglet Nour dates.
kebili.c: A good base from which to explore the chott and the desert; intense heat in summer.
kebili.d: Capital of the Kebili governorate in the Nefzaoua region, one of the oldest oases in Tunisia and North Africa, near Chott el-Jerid. Deglet Nour dates.

kerkouane.a: The complete plan of the Punic city with streets and houses; the pink-coloured baths of the private bathing quarters; the small museum and the rock-cut necropolis.
kerkouane.c: The only purely Punic city to have been preserved; best visited in conjunction with the Cap Bon coast and Kelibia.
kerkouane.d: A Punic city abandoned around the 3rd century BC and never rebuilt, a rare example of Phoenician-Punic urban planning. Listed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
kerkouane.h: Site managed by the AMVPPC — open during the day; opening hours vary according to the season; please check on site.

koubba de sidi el mezri (monastir).a: Shrine and koubba of the saint Sidi Mezri (died in 1141), in the heart of the large seaside cemetery of the same name, near the ribat.
koubba de sidi el mezri (monastir).c: Worth seeing whilst strolling between the ribat and Bourguiba’s mausoleum.
koubba de sidi el mezri (monastir).d: The shrine and koubba of Saint Sidi Mezri (died 1141), within the large seaside cemetery of Sidi El Mezri near the ribat. Approximate coordinates.

ksar beni barka.a: Ksar with ghorfas, a former communal granary for the tribes of the Tataouine region.
ksar beni barka.c: Short visit; can be combined with the other nearby ksours of the Dahar.
ksar beni barka.d: Fortified ksar with ghorfas in the Tataouine governorate, formerly a communal granary for the region’s tribes.

ksar beni ghedir.a: Ksar a Ghorfas in the north of Tataouine, in the area of the fortified granaries of Dahar.
ksar beni ghedir.c: A short stop; worth including in a tour of the ksours.
ksar beni ghedir.d: Ksar a Ghorfas in the north of the Tataouine governorate, in the area of the fortified granaries of Dahar.

ksar beni mhira (el ataya).a: A rectangular ksar (150 x 70 m) on a hill in the Djeffara region, with around 160 ghorfas.
ksar beni mhira (el ataya).c: A pleasant vantage point for watching the sunset; bring water.
ksar beni mhira (el ataya).d: Rectangular ksar (150x70 m) on a hill in the Djeffara, ~160 ghorfas.

ksar beni mhira (zorgane).a: A parallelogram-shaped ksar (120x80 m) with 170 to 250 ghorfas spread over two storeys.
ksar beni mhira (zorgane).c: Best visited in conjunction with the other Beni Mhira ksar; expect hot weather.
ksar beni mhira (zorgane).d: A parallelogram-shaped ksar (120x80 m) near Beni Mhira, with 170 to 250 ghorfas on two storeys.

ksar dghaghra.a: Berber ksar (fortified granary) in the Tataouine governorate.
ksar dghaghra.c: A quick visit; can be combined with the neighbouring ksours of Dahar.
ksar dghaghra.d: Berber ksar (fortified granary) in the Tataouine governorate.

ksar el kedim.a: A listed fortified ksar, attributed to the Zenete Berbers, in the Tataouine governorate.
ksar el kedim.c: A modest site to include in a tour of the ksours with a local guide.
ksar el kedim.d: Fortified ksar in the governorate of Tataouine, a listed monument, attributed to the Zenete Berbers.

ksar ezzahra.a: A mountain ksar at the foot of Djebel Abiodh, with a square-shaped old quarter and a more recent Ksar Jedid; listed as a monument.
ksar ezzahra.c: Access via the mountains to the south-east of Tataouine: drive carefully and take water with you.
ksar ezzahra.d: Mountain ksar at the foot of Djebel Abiodh, south-east of Tataouine, with a square old quarter and the more recent Ksar Jedid. Listed as a monument in January 2024.

ksar hadada.a: Partially restored Ksar a Ghorfas, north of Tataouine near Ghomrassen.
ksar hadada.c: A quick visit is possible; can be combined with the neighbouring ksours in the Ghomrassen region.
ksar hadada.d: Ksar a Ghorfas, north of Tataouine (Ghomrassen region), partially restored.

ksar hallouf.a: A fortified ksar stands on a hill overlooking the valley, in the Beni Khedache region.
ksar hallouf.c: Mountain road: drive carefully and take water to cope with the heat.
ksar hallouf.d: A fortified ksar in the Medenine region (Beni Khedache), standing on a hill overlooking the valley.

ksar jelidet (ksar boujlida).a: A listed Berber fort-granary, forming part of the Ksour Jelidet complex.
ksar jelidet (ksar boujlida).c: Access via tracks: a local guide makes it easier to find.
ksar jelidet (ksar boujlida).d: A ksar forming part of the Ksour Jelidet complex, a listed Berber fortified granary.

ksar jouamaa.a: Fortified communal granary built of Beni Khedache stone, constructed around 1770.
ksar jouamaa.c: Mountain site: bring water and footwear suitable for the terrain.
ksar jouamaa.d: Stone ksar at Beni Khedache (Medenine), built around 1770. Fortified communal granary listed as a Tunisian monument.

ksar lemsa (limisa).a: A remarkably well-preserved 6th-century Byzantine fortress, with its almost intact large-stone walls overlooking the valley, set amongst the ruins of Limisa.
ksar lemsa (limisa).c: Site on the outskirts of Siliana (Oueslatia area): the fortress can be explored in under an hour and offers a fine view of the valley.
ksar lemsa (limisa).d: A remarkably well-preserved 6th-century Byzantine fortress, set amongst the ruins of the ancient Roman-Berber city of Limisa. In Oueslatia (Kairouan), on the border with Siliana, it overlooks the valley with its almost intact large-stone walls.

ksar megabla.a: An oval-shaped ksar on the outskirts of Tataouine, with numerous ghorfas on two to four levels.
ksar megabla.c: A short stop just outside Tataouine; expect hot weather.
ksar megabla.d: An oval-shaped ksar on the outskirts of Tataouine, founded around 1400, with numerous ghorfas on two to four levels.

ksar ouled aoun.a: A semi-circular ksar with ghorfas near Maztouria, restored, with two to three storeys.
ksar ouled aoun.c: A short stop; the light at the end of the day is most flattering for photos.
ksar ouled aoun.d: The semi-circular Ksar a Ghorfas near Maztouria, with 96 to 220 ghorfas spread over two to three storeys; restored in 2007.

ksar ouled brahim (medenine).a: A square ksar measuring approximately 80 m on each side, with around 140 vaulted ghorfas on two levels, a fine example of Medenine’s ksar district.
ksar ouled brahim (medenine).c: In town: accessible on foot whilst visiting Medenine.
ksar ouled brahim (medenine).d: Ksar in the centre of Medenine, square in plan, approximately 80 m on each side, with around 140 vaulted ghorfas on two levels. A fine example of the town’s ksar district.

ksar ouled debbab.a: Fortified ksar with ghorfas, partly cave-dwelling, situated on a hill near Tataouine; designated a national monument.
ksar ouled debbab.c: Unobstructed view from the ksar: the late afternoon light is the most beautiful.
ksar ouled debbab.d: Fortified ksar at Ghorfas near Tataouine, partly cave-dwelling, situated on a hilltop. Designated a national monument in January 2024.

ksar ouled m'hemed.a: Fortified granary with ghorfas (circa 1855) comprising approximately 223 cells on three levels, restored in collaboration with the INP.
ksar ouled m'hemed.c: Quick visit; can be combined with the neighbouring ksours of Tataouine.
ksar ouled m'hemed.d: Fortified granary with ghorfas (Tataouine), built around 1855, with ~223 cells on three levels. Restored in 2007 with the INP.

ksar ouled soltane.a: One of the best-preserved ksour with ghorfas in the south, its storage cells stacked over several storeys around courtyards.
ksar ouled soltane.c: Lighting and photo opportunities are best at the end of the day; the site is managed by the AMVPPC – opening times should be checked on site.
ksar ouled soltane.d: A Berber ksar with ghorfas (multi-storey storage cells) south of Tataouine, among the best-preserved in southern Tunisia.
ksar ouled soltane.h: Site managed by the AMVPPC — open during the day; opening hours vary according to the season, to be checked on site.

ksar tamelest.a: Former fortified granary with ghorfas in the Dahar region, in the Tataouine governorate.
ksar tamelest.c: A modest site; best included as part of a guided tour of the ksours of the Dahar.
ksar tamelest.d: A ksar with ghorfas in the Tataouine governorate, a former fortified granary in the Dahar region.

la goulette (halq el oued).a: The seafront and the harbour, the seafood restaurants on the main avenue and the traces of the cosmopolitan past (Italian and Jewish quarters) of the former outer harbour of Tunis.
la goulette (halq el oued).c: Ideal for a midday meal of grilled fish; accessible by TGM from Tunis.
la goulette (halq el oued).d: A port town at the entrance to Lake Tunis, the capital’s historic outer harbour. A fishing district with a cosmopolitan past.

lac de bizerte.a: A vast coastal lagoon connected to the Mediterranean and Lake Ichkeul by channels. On its shores lie the old port of Bizerte, its kasbah and the canal – one of the most beautiful ports in the north.
lac de bizerte.c: Best explored by car or viewed from the shores; combine with the nearby Ichkeul Park and the old port of Bizerte.
lac de bizerte.d: A coastal lagoon connected to the Mediterranean and Lake Ichkeul by channels. A sheltered body of water in the north of the country.

lac de tunis.a: A lagoon on the outskirts of the capital: flamingos and waders around the islet of Chikly, which is home to the 16th-century Borj Chikly fort. The La Goulette road crosses the lake, offering views of Tunis; on the Lac 1 side, there is a landscaped promenade and waterside cafés.
lac de tunis.c: Birdwatching in winter; binoculars are useful; beautiful light in the morning from the shores. Borj Chikly (islet) can only be visited occasionally, by boat.
lac de tunis.d: A brackish lagoon between Tunis and the Gulf of Tunis, separated from the sea by a coastal sandbar. A wetland home to flamingos and waders.

lac ichkeul.a: National Park (UNESCO, Ramsar): walking trails, an ecological museum, and above all the birdlife — flamingos, storks, pelicans, and thousands of coots and ducks overwintering here (229 animal species recorded). At the foot of the djebel (511 m), there are hot springs and traditional hammams, with Roman ruins nearby.
lac ichkeul.c: Visit early in the morning or late in the afternoon (to avoid the heat); the best time for birdwatching is from October to February. Access to the national park is regulated: check with the forestry authorities (Eaux & Forêts / DGF).
lac ichkeul.d: A brackish lake connected to the Bizerte lagoon, at the heart of Ichkeul National Park. A Ramsar site and UNESCO World Heritage Site.

lagune de ghar el melh.a: The Ramsar lagoon and wetland at the foot of Djebel Nadhour, renowned for its traditional ramli gardens and birdlife.
lagune de ghar el melh.c: Beautiful light at the end of the day; bring binoculars for birdwatching and visit the town’s Ottoman forts whilst you’re there.
lagune de ghar el melh.d: A coastal lagoon and wetland at the foot of Djebel Nadhour, a Ramsar site renowned for its ramli gardens and birdlife. Coordinates centred on the village.

lagune de korba (sebkha korba).a: Coastal lagoon north of Korba, an important wetland for migratory birds of Cap Bon.
lagune de korba (sebkha korba).c: Birdwatching site; the migration periods are the best times to visit; binoculars are useful.
lagune de korba (sebkha korba).d: Coastal lagoon north of Korba, an important wetland for migratory birds of Cap Bon.

le galiton.a: The rocky islet with a lighthouse, Tunisia’s westernmost point, in the La Galite archipelago.
le galiton.c: A remote site out at sea: best viewed during a boat trip around La Galite.
le galiton.d: A rocky islet in the La Galite archipelago featuring a lighthouse, the westernmost point of Tunisia.

le kef (kasbah et medina).a: The Ottoman kasbah overlooking the town, the medina with its mosques and zaouias, and the early Christian basilica of Dar El Kous, all built on top of the ancient Sicca Veneria.
le kef (kasbah et medina).c: A hilltop town that is pleasant to explore on foot; allow half a day and make sure you have good shoes for the sloping alleyways.
le kef (kasbah et medina).d: A hilltop town in the north-west dominated by its Ottoman kasbah, built on top of the ancient Sicca Veneria. A complex of mosques, zaouias and a basilica.

le lezard rouge (train historique de met.a: Metre-gauge tourist train, featuring the Bey’s historic rolling stock, which winds its way through the Selja Gorges.
le lezard rouge (train historique de met.c: Book in advance during peak season and bring plenty of water; departs from Metlaoui.
le lezard rouge (train historique de met.d: Metre-gauge tourist train running through the Selja Gorges between Metlaoui and Redeyef, on the former phosphate mining line. Rolling stock from a former Bey’s train. Station coordinates (approximate).

le sers.a: A town in a grain-growing region, with no major monuments, on the plain to the south-east of El Kef.
le sers.c: A simple stop-off on the road; of little tourist interest in its own right.
le sers.d: A town about 35 km south-east of El Kef, in a grain-growing region.

leptiminus (leptis minor).a: The remains of the ancient harbour and thermal baths; the small museum displaying local pottery and mosaics.
leptiminus (leptis minor).c: A quiet site in Lamta, for archaeology enthusiasts, best visited in conjunction with the nearby ribat.
leptiminus (leptis minor).d: Ancient city corresponding to present-day Lamta, founded around 500 BC. Centre of a prosperous Roman olive-growing district: Punic tombs, amphitheatre, thermal baths, aqueducts. Approximate coordinates.

ligne mareth.a: Remains of fortifications in southern Tunisia, breached by the British 8th Army in March 1943.
ligne mareth.c: Landmarks scattered across the plain: a guide or the Mareth Museum can help locate them.
ligne mareth.d: A system of fortifications in southern Tunisia built by the French to face Italian-occupied Libya, captured by the Axis powers in 1942–1943. Breached by the British 8th Army in March 1943. Approximate coordinates.

limes tripolitanus (frontiere saharienne.a: A network of Roman forts, outposts and tracks controlling the Saharan frontier; scattered remains in the pre-Saharan region.
limes tripolitanus (frontiere saharienne.c: Extensive, desert-like area: a 4x4 vehicle, a guide and a supply of water are essential.
limes tripolitanus (frontiere saharienne.d: A system of fortifications and tracks controlling the southern border of Roman Africa (outposts, forts, centenaria) in the pre-Saharan region. Approximate coordinates for a sector.

m'saken.a: A town in the Sahel with a rich heritage: the Great Mosque, the El Aousat Mosque, the Chakir Saheb Ettabaâ Palace (1828) and numerous zaouias.
m'saken.c: An urban stroll off the beaten track; visits are mainly of the exterior.
m'saken.d: A town in the Sahel region south of Sousse: the Great Mosque, the El Aousat Mosque, the Chakir Saheb Ettabaâ Palace (1828) and numerous zaouias.

magel bel abbes.a: A town in the far south-west of Kasserine, near the Algerian border.
magel bel abbes.c: Border area: check access details before travelling there.
magel bel abbes.d: A town in the far south-west of the Kasserine governorate, near the Algerian border.

mahboubine (djerba).a: A village in south-eastern Djerba, known for its Ottoman-inspired El Kateb Mosque.
mahboubine (djerba).c: A short stop to admire the mosque; please dress appropriately when visiting.
mahboubine (djerba).d: A village in south-eastern Djerba, known for its Ottoman-inspired El Kateb Mosque.

mahdia (medina et site historique).a: the monumental Skifa Kahla gate; the reconstructed Fatimid Great Mosque; the Borj el-Kebir; the maritime cemetery and Cape Afrique.
mahdia (medina et site historique).c: Take a stroll around the peninsula at sunset; the fishing harbour comes to life early in the morning.
mahdia (medina et site historique).d: Former Fatimid capital founded in the 10th century on a fortified peninsula, featuring its monumental gate (Skifa Kahla) and its grand mosque.

maison d'amphitrite (bulla regia).a: The underground dwelling, famous for its Amphitrite mosaic which remains in situ, is a remarkable example of Bulla Regia’s troglodytic dwellings.
maison d'amphitrite (bulla regia).c: Head down into the underground chamber to admire the mosaic, which is cooler during the hottest part of the day; don’t miss it.
maison d'amphitrite (bulla regia).d: The underground dwelling at Bulla Regia, famous for its mosaic of Amphitrite. Cave-dwelling architecture.

maison de la cascade (utique).a: The Roman domus, adorned with mosaics and featuring a pool, is one of the finest residential complexes at the Utica site.
maison de la cascade (utique).c: Included in the tour of the Utica site; take a look at the mosaics in situ around the pool.
maison de la cascade (utique).d: Roman domus at the Utica site, decorated with mosaics and featuring a pool.

maison de la chasse (bulla regia).a: The semi-underground Roman house adorned with mosaics, typical of the underground dwellings at Bulla Regia.
maison de la chasse (bulla regia).c: Combine this with a visit to the neighbouring House of Amphitrite whilst touring the underground villas.
maison de la chasse (bulla regia).d: Semi-underground Roman dwelling at Bulla Regia, decorated with mosaics, typical of the underground dwellings.

makthar (mactaris).a: Trajan’s Arch, the well-preserved Great Southern Baths, the ‘House of Venus’ and the Schola des Juvenes, set against the backdrop of the high steppe.
makthar (mactaris).c: Make sure you bring water and sturdy shoes as the site is extensive and exposed; the visit takes around 2 hours and is particularly pleasant in spring.
makthar (mactaris).d: An ancient city of Numidian origin that later became Roman, featuring Trajan’s Arch, the Great Southern Baths and the ‘House of Venus’. Situated at high altitude in the high steppe.
makthar (mactaris).h: Site managed by the AMVPPC — open during the day; opening hours vary according to the season, so please check on site.

marais salants de monastir.a: A wetland of around 1,000 ha designated a Ramsar site in 2012, important for pink flamingos.
marais salants de monastir.c: A good spot for observing flamingos; come early in the morning with binoculars.
marais salants de monastir.d: Wetland (~1,000 ha) designated a Ramsar site in 2012, important for pink flamingos.

marais salants de thyna (sfax).a: Salt pans and coastal wetland south of Sfax (Ramsar), important for flamingos and waterbirds.
marais salants de thyna (sfax).c: Bring binoculars; observe from the dykes without disturbing the birds.
marais salants de thyna (sfax).d: Salt pans and coastal wetland south of Sfax, along the Gulf of Gabès near Thyna. Large protected wetland, designated a Ramsar site in 2007, important for waterbirds. Approximate coordinates.

marche romain (macellum) de musti / el k.a: An ancient covered market made of white limestone, situated at the heart of the site alongside the forum, temples and cisterns.
marche romain (macellum) de musti / el k.c: Worth seeing whilst exploring Musti; this particular spot can be viewed in just a few minutes.
marche romain (macellum) de musti / el k.d: Covered market (macellum) of ancient Musti, built of white limestone, at the heart of the site alongside the forum, temples and cisterns. Coordinates within the site are approximate.

mareth.a: A town that gave its name to the Mareth Line; a local museum commemorates the battle of 1943.
mareth.c: The Mareth Line Museum helps visitors to understand the surrounding ruins.
mareth.d: A town between Gabès and Medenine, which gave its name to the Mareth Line (1930s).

masculula (henchir guergour).a: The ruins of ancient Masculula, where Neo-Punic and Latin inscriptions were found (some of which are in the Louvre).
masculula (henchir guergour).c: A rural site near Touiref, largely undeveloped: best left to epigraphy enthusiasts with the exact coordinates.
masculula (henchir guergour).d: The ruins of ancient Masculula near Touiref, where Neo-Punic and Latin inscriptions were discovered (some of which are in the Louvre).

matmata.a: Village known for its cave dwellings carved into the ground in a crater-like formation, arranged around circular courtyards.
matmata.c: Some houses are open to visitors; please respect the residents’ privacy and avoid visiting during the hottest part of the day.
matmata.d: A Berber village known for its cave dwellings carved into the ground in a crater-like formation. Coordinates of the village centre.

mausolee de bourguiba (monastir).a: the mausoleum with its gilded dome and minarets; the marble courtyard and the esplanade; the monumental cemetery.
mausolee de bourguiba (monastir).c: Best visited in conjunction with the nearby ribat; please dress respectfully at this place of remembrance.
mausolee de bourguiba (monastir).d: The mausoleum of Habib Bourguiba, the first president of the Tunisian Republic, designed by Olivier-Clement Cacoub. Two minarets and a gilded dome. Approximate coordinates.

mausolee des flavii (cillium).a: A three-storey tower-mausoleum from the mid-2nd century, bearing the longest surviving epigraphic poem from the Roman world.
mausolee des flavii (cillium).c: The most prominent landmark in the ancient district of Cillium; a quick visit worth including in your trip to Kasserine.
mausolee des flavii (cillium).d: A three-storey tower-mausoleum erected around the middle of the 2nd century near Kasserine, bearing the longest surviving epigraphic poem from the Roman world.

mausolee el ouhaichia.a: Zaouïa-mausoleum in the medina of Kairouan; a modest monument.
mausolee el ouhaichia.c: Worth a look whilst strolling through the medina.
mausolee el ouhaichia.d: Zaouïa-mausoleum in the medina of Kairouan.

mausolee omar makhlouf (monastir).a: Zaouïa and mausoleum in the medina of Monastir, a traditional place of worship.
mausolee omar makhlouf (monastir).c: A small building worth seeing whilst passing through the medina; please respect the religious nature of the site.
mausolee omar makhlouf (monastir).d: Zaouïa and mausoleum in the medina of Monastir, a traditional place of worship.

mausolee sidi abdesselam.a: Zaouïa-mausoleum in the medina of Kairouan; a modest monument.
mausolee sidi abdesselam.c: Worth a look whilst strolling through the medina.
mausolee sidi abdesselam.d: Zaouïa-mausoleum in the medina of Kairouan.

mausolee sidi ali azouz (tebourba).a: The zaouïa and mausoleum of the Sufi saint, with its traditional décor, in the heart of Tebourba’s old town.
mausolee sidi ali azouz (tebourba).c: Appropriate attire is required; a brief spiritual stop in the old town centre.
mausolee sidi ali azouz (tebourba).d: Zaouïa and mausoleum of a Sufi saint in Tebourba, in the heart of the old town.

mausolee sidi amor abbada.a: A 19th-century zaouïa known as the Mosque of the Sabres, recognisable by its five fluted domes and its monumental features.
mausolee sidi amor abbada.c: A place of interest to include on a walk around Kairouan; modest dress is appreciated.
mausolee sidi amor abbada.d: The Zaouïa of Sidi Amor Abbada (Mosque of the Sabres), 19th century, recognisable by its five fluted domes.

mdhilla.a: Phosphate mining town in the governorate of Gafsa, home to the CPG plant.
mdhilla.c: Industrial town: of little interest to visitors.
mdhilla.d: Phosphate mining town in the governorate of Gafsa (CPG plant).

medenine (ville et ksour).a: Capital city famous for its ksour a ghorfas, ancient communal storehouses of the Berber tribes.
medenine (ville et ksour).c: A few restored ghorfas can be visited in the town; a convenient stopover on the way to the ksour of Dahar.
medenine (ville et ksour).d: Capital of the Medenine governorate, famous for its ksour a ghorfas (collective storehouses of the Berber tribes).

medersa slimania.a: The courtyard with its two-tone arches; the row of three madrasas on Rue des Libraires.
medersa slimania.c: On the way between the Zitouna and the souks. Check opening times on arrival.
medersa slimania.d: A Koranic school founded in 1754 by Ali I Pasha in memory of his son Slimane. Situated very close to the Zitouna, on Rue des Libraires, it is organised around a porticoed courtyard with black-and-white painted arches, flanked by the cells where the students lived.

medina de gabes (jara).a: The historic heart of the oasis town on the Gulf, with the old quarters of Petite and Grande Jara, on the site of ancient Tacapae.
medina de gabes (jara).c: Stroll through the medina and the neighbouring oasis, avoiding the midday heat.
medina de gabes (jara).d: The historic centre of Gabès, an oasis town in the gulf, with the old quarters of Petite and Grande Jara, on the site of ancient Tacapae.

medina de kairouan.a: The Great Mosque; the Aghlabid Fountains; the Zaouïa of Sidi Sahbi (Barber’s Mosque); the carpet souks and the Mosque of the Three Gates.
medina de kairouan.c: Buy the combined ticket giving access to the main monuments; this is a holy city, so modest dress is appreciated.
medina de kairouan.d: The historic heart of Kairouan, a holy city of Islam founded in 670, surrounded by ramparts and home to the Great Mosque and numerous monuments. A UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1988. Approximate coordinates.

medina de sfax.a: The medieval ramparts and Bab Diwan; the covered souks, which are still very lively; the Great Mosque; the kasbah and the Heritage Museum.
medina de sfax.c: One of the most authentic medinas, with few tourists; enter via Bab Diwan and follow the craft souks.
medina de sfax.d: The historic centre of Sfax, founded by the Aghlabids around 849–851, is one of the few medieval towns in the Maghreb to have preserved its urban layout and ramparts. UNESCO Tentative List.

medina de sousse.a: the crenellated ramparts; the ribat and its watchtower; the kasbah, home to the museum and its mosaics; the Great Mosque.
medina de sousse.c: Climb up to the ribat tower or the kasbah for views of the medina and the harbour.
medina de sousse.d: The fortified medina of Sousse with its ramparts, kasbah, ribat and grand mosque. Listed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

medina de tunis.a: The Zitouna Mosque; the covered souks (perfumers, chechias); the Dar Hussein and Dar Lasram palaces; the Bab Bhar and Bab Jedid gates; the panoramic terraces of the cafés.
medina de tunis.c: Lose yourself here in the morning when the souks come to life; head up to a café terrace for views of the minarets.
medina de tunis.d: The historic heart of Tunis, founded in the 7th–9th centuries, with a dense network of souks, mosques and palaces. Listed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

medjez el-bab.a: The strategic town on the Medjerda, its historic crossing point and traces of the 1942–1943 Tunisian campaign.
medjez el-bab.c: To be combined with the Ottoman bridge and the Commonwealth Memorial; a stopover for military and river history.
medjez el-bab.d: A strategic town on the Medjerda, a historic crossing point and a key location in the Tunisian campaign (1942–1943).

memorial de medjez el-bab.a: The Commonwealth Memorial honouring soldiers who went missing during the Tunisian Campaign and have no known grave.
memorial de medjez el-bab.c: A place of reflection; a quiet, short visit, to be combined with the bridge and the town of Medjez el-Bab.
memorial de medjez el-bab.d: Commonwealth Memorial honouring soldiers from the Tunisian Campaign who are missing and have no known grave.

meninx.a: Djerba’s main ancient city, once renowned for its purple dye: remains of the forum and ruins of buildings in the south of the island.
meninx.c: An open-air archaeological site, largely undeveloped: closed-toe shoes and water are recommended.
meninx.d: The main ancient city on the island of Djerba, renowned in antiquity for its production of purple dye. Remains of the forum and amphitheatre.

metameur (ksar).a: A village whose ksar, with its vaulted ghorfas on several levels, is one of the best-preserved in the south.
metameur (ksar).c: 7 km from Medenine, an easy stop; photogenic light at the end of the day.
metameur (ksar).d: A village approximately 7 km north-west of Medenine, founded around the 14th century, renowned for its ksar with vaulted ghorfas on several levels. One of the best-preserved in the south.

metlaoui.a: A mining town in the Gafsa Basin, the starting point for the Lezard Rouge train to the Selja Gorges.
metlaoui.c: Book the Lezard Rouge in advance; water is essential in summer.
metlaoui.d: A mining town in the Gafsa Basin (phosphate), the departure point for the Lezard Rouge train to the Selja Gorges.

metline.a: The coastal village of Andalusian origin to the north-east of Bizerte, with its maritime and wine-growing heritage.
metline.c: A peaceful stopover to combine with Raf Raf and the other Andalusian villages along the coast.
metline.d: A coastal village of Andalusian origin to the north-east of Bizerte (maritime and wine-growing heritage).

midoun (djerba).a: Djerba’s second-largest town, a lively hub in the north-east of the island.
midoun (djerba).c: Famous weekly market: arrive early to soak up the atmosphere and avoid the heat.
midoun (djerba).d: Djerba’s second-largest town by population, the centre of the north-east of the island.

missua (site antique de sidi daoud).a: Ancient Punic and Roman ruins at Sidi Daoud, on the north coast of Cap Bon.
missua (site antique de sidi daoud).c: Location is imprecise and the site is poorly developed; best suited to enthusiasts.
missua (site antique de sidi daoud).d: The ancient archaeological site of Missua, at Sidi Daoud on Cape Bon. Wikidata coordinates are of low accuracy (~1 km) and approximate.

monts de matmata.a: The Dahar range, known for its cave dwellings and arid landscapes.
monts de matmata.c: Scenic but winding roads: drive carefully and carry water.
monts de matmata.d: The Dahar range in southern Tunisia, known for its cave dwellings and arid landscapes. Coordinates centred on Matmata.

mosquee al malek (kairouan).a: Historic mosque in the medina of Kairouan.
mosquee al malek (kairouan).c: Place of worship: view from the outside and keep a low profile.
mosquee al malek (kairouan).d: Historic mosque in the medina of Kairouan.

mosquee bourguiba de monastir.a: The Great Hanafi Mosque, built in 1963 and inspired by the Hammouda Pasha Mosque in Tunis, is located in the medina of Monastir.
mosquee bourguiba de monastir.c: Visits are permitted outside prayer times; appropriate attire is required.
mosquee bourguiba de monastir.d: The Great Hanafi Mosque of Monastir, dedicated to Bourguiba, built in 1963 (architect Taieb Bouzguenda), inspired by the Hammouda Pasha Mosque in Tunis. Approximate coordinates.

mosquee d'el may (djerba).a: Fortified Ibadite mosque with whitewashed walls and a stocky minaret, listed since 1928.
mosquee d'el may (djerba).c: Be sure to admire the fortified exterior; the interior may be reserved for worshippers.
mosquee d'el may (djerba).d: A fortified Ibadite mosque in the centre of Djerba, with whitewashed walls and a stocky minaret. Listed as a historic monument in 1928, it serves the defensive role typical of the island’s mosques.

mosquee de bab teboursouk (testour).a: The Andalusian-style mosque near the Teboursouk Gate, part of Testour’s Moorish heritage.
mosquee de bab teboursouk (testour).c: Well worth seeing whilst strolling through Testour, along with the Great Andalusian Mosque; appropriate dress required.
mosquee de bab teboursouk (testour).d: The Andalusian-style Testour Mosque, near the Teboursouk Gate, a legacy of the Moriscos.

mosquee de djerba (architecture djerbien.a: Typical Djerbian architecture: whitewashed walls, rounded domes and clean lines.
mosquee de djerba (architecture djerbien.c: Access to the interior may be restricted to worshippers; be sure to admire the white walls bathed in low-angled light.
mosquee de djerba (architecture djerbien.d: A traditional mosque in the Djerban architectural style, with whitewashed walls and domes characteristic of the island.

mosquee de la kasbah.a: The 13th-century Hafsid minaret, a model for Tunisian religious architecture, overlooking Kasbah Square above the medina.
mosquee de la kasbah.c: Best viewed from the outside from the square; best visited in combination with the nearby Dar El Bey.
mosquee de la kasbah.d: The Kasbah Mosque in Tunis, founded in the 13th century under the Hafsids, whose minaret served as a model for Tunisian religious architecture.

mosquee des trois portes.a: The 9th-century Aghlabid façade adorned with carved Kufic inscriptions, one of the oldest dated mosque façades.
mosquee des trois portes.c: A small monument in the narrow streets of Kairouan, worth seeing whilst exploring the medina.
mosquee des trois portes.d: Mosque founded in 866 by Mohammed ibn Khairoun, in the medina of Kairouan. The oldest carved and decorated façade in the Islamic world; Hafsid minaret added around 1440.

mosquee el lawlib (kairouan).a: Historic mosque in the medina of Kairouan.
mosquee el lawlib (kairouan).c: Place of worship: view from the outside and remain discreet.
mosquee el lawlib (kairouan).d: Historic mosque in the medina of Kairouan.

mosquee el trouk (sfax).a: Ottoman mosque in the medina of Sfax, a reminder of the Turkish era.
mosquee el trouk (sfax).c: Place of worship: view from the outside and remain discreet.
mosquee el trouk (sfax).d: Historic mosque in the medina of Sfax.

mosquee fadhloun (djerba).a: A 14th-century Ibadite mosque with simple, fortified architecture, on the outskirts of Midoun.
mosquee fadhloun (djerba).c: A beautiful, isolated white silhouette: ideal for photographing in soft light.
mosquee fadhloun (djerba).d: A 14th-century Ibadite mosque on the outskirts of Midoun, with the simple, fortified architecture typical of Djerba. Listed in 2022.

mosquee hammouda pacha.a: the Ottoman-inspired octagonal minaret; the marble decoration and the courtyard; the mausoleum of the founding bey.
mosquee hammouda pacha.c: Worth seeing whilst strolling through the Medina of Tunis.
mosquee hammouda pacha.d: Hanafi mosque in the Medina of Tunis (early 17th century), with an Ottoman-style octagonal minaret. It houses the tourbet of the Mouradite family.

mosquee rebaa (bizerte).a: Historic Ottoman-era mosque in the heart of Bizerte’s medina.
mosquee rebaa (bizerte).c: Appropriate attire is required; best viewed whilst strolling through the medina, as there is no specific route to follow.
mosquee rebaa (bizerte).d: Historic mosque in the medina of Bizerte.

mosquee saheb ettabaa.a: This early 19th-century complex, comprising a mosque, madrasa and mausoleum, features marble and stucco decoration and is situated in the north of the medina.
mosquee saheb ettabaa.c: Best visited in combination with the Saheb Ettabaa Palace and the Halfaouine district.
mosquee saheb ettabaa.d: Religious complex in the north of the medina of Tunis (early 19th century) founded by Youssef Saheb Ettabaa: mosque, madrasa and mausoleum.

mosquee sidi abdelmoula.a: Historic mosque in the medina of Sfax.
mosquee sidi abdelmoula.c: Place of worship: view from the outside and be discreet.
mosquee sidi abdelmoula.d: Historic mosque in the medina of Sfax.

mosquee sidi achour (nabeul).a: The historic mosque in Nabeul, listed as a historic monument since 1915.
mosquee sidi achour (nabeul).c: Mainly an exterior visit; best included as part of a stroll through the medina.
mosquee sidi achour (nabeul).d: The Sidi Achour Mosque in Nabeul, listed as a historic monument since 3 March 1915.

mosquee sidi amar kammoun.a: Historic mosque in the Sfax medina.
mosquee sidi amar kammoun.c: Place of worship: view from the outside and keep a low profile.
mosquee sidi amar kammoun.d: Historic mosque in the medina of Sfax.

mosquee sidi ellakhmi.a: Historic mosque in the medina of Sfax.
mosquee sidi ellakhmi.c: Place of worship: view from the outside and remain discreet.
mosquee sidi ellakhmi.d: Historic mosque in the medina of Sfax.

mosquee sidi elyes (sfax).a: Historic mosque in the medina of Sfax.
mosquee sidi elyes (sfax).c: Place of worship: view from the outside and be discreet.
mosquee sidi elyes (sfax).d: Historic mosque in the medina of Sfax.

mosquee sidi mahrez (tunis).a: the ensemble of white domes inspired by the Ottoman style of Istanbul, unique to Tunis; the zaouïa of the patron saint opposite.
mosquee sidi mahrez (tunis).c: A striking silhouette visible from the narrow streets of the Bab Souika district.
mosquee sidi mahrez (tunis).d: Ottoman-era mosque in the medina of Tunis, notable for its Ottoman-inspired domes, dedicated to the city’s patron saint.

mosquee sikaya (kairouan).a: The historic mosque in the medina of Kairouan.
mosquee sikaya (kairouan).c: Place of worship: view from the outside and be discreet.
mosquee sikaya (kairouan).d: Historic mosque in the medina of Kairouan.

mosquee zitouna (grande mosquee de tunis.a: The large prayer hall with its reused ancient columns; the vast paved courtyard and its sundial; the minaret.
mosquee zitouna (grande mosquee de tunis.c: Modest dress required; the courtyard is open to non-Muslim visitors during the day.
mosquee zitouna (grande mosquee de tunis.d: The Great Mosque and the main religious monument of the Medina of Tunis, founded during the Umayyad/Aghlabid period, and long a centre of learning.
mosquee zitouna (grande mosquee de tunis.h: Place of worship — visits possible during opening hours; appropriate attire required.

moulares (oum el araies).a: Phosphate mining town about 50 km from Gafsa, near the Algerian border.
moulares (oum el araies).d: Phosphate mining town (Oum El Araies) about 50 km from Gafsa, near the Algerian border.

musee archeologique d'el jem (maison d'a.a: A rich collection of mosaics near the amphitheatre, with a park featuring Roman villas, including the reconstructed House of Africa.
musee archeologique d'el jem (maison d'a.c: Combine this with a visit to the nearby amphitheatre to gain an understanding of ancient Thysdrus.
musee archeologique d'el jem (maison d'a.d: Museum near the amphitheatre at El Jem (Thysdrus), with a significant collection of mosaics. Park featuring Roman villas, including the reconstructed House of Africa.
musee archeologique d'el jem (maison d'a.h: Museum — open during the day (may be closed one day a week); check opening times on site.

musee archeologique de gafsa.a: Collections of Capsian tools (stone and bone), Roman artefacts and mosaics from ancient Capsa.
musee archeologique de gafsa.c: A welcome, air-conditioned stop during the hottest part of the day; opening times to be checked on site.
musee archeologique de gafsa.d: The Gafsa Medina Museum, rich in Capsian stone and bone tools, as well as Roman artefacts and mosaics from ancient Capsa. Approximate coordinates.
musee archeologique de gafsa.h: Museum — open during the day (may be closed one day a week); opening times to be checked on site.

musee archeologique de lamta.a: A seaside museum on the site of ancient Leptiminus, tracing the local history from the Phoenicians through to the Roman and early Christian periods.
musee archeologique de lamta.c: This visit is best combined with a visit to the neighbouring Ribat of Lamta.
musee archeologique de lamta.d: The museum opened in 1992, situated by the sea at the site of ancient Leptiminus. It houses collections spanning from the arrival of the Phoenicians through to the Roman and early Christian periods.
musee archeologique de lamta.h: Museum — open during the day (may be closed one day a week); check opening times on site.

musee archeologique de salakta.a: Museum displaying the remains of ancient Sullecthum, including a large mosaic of a lion.
musee archeologique de salakta.c: Best visited alongside the nearby Salakta archaeological site.
musee archeologique de salakta.d: The Salakta Archaeological Museum, showcasing the remains of ancient Sullecthum.
musee archeologique de salakta.h: Museum — open during the day (may be closed one day a week); check opening times on site.

musee archeologique de sbeitla.a: Mosaics and artefacts dating from prehistoric times to the Islamic period, opposite the Sufetula site.
musee archeologique de sbeitla.c: A short visit (~45 mins) to combine with the archaeological site directly opposite.
musee archeologique de sbeitla.d: Museum in Sbeitla, opposite the archaeological site, featuring mosaics and artefacts from prehistoric times to the Islamic period.
musee archeologique de sbeitla.h: Museum — open during the day (may be closed one day a week); check opening times on arrival.

musee archeologique de sfax.a: The city museum displays ancient collections from the region, including mosaics.
musee archeologique de sfax.c: A good introduction before exploring the medina and the surrounding ancient sites.
musee archeologique de sfax.d: Archaeological Museum of the city of Sfax.
musee archeologique de sfax.h: Museum — open during the day (may be closed one day a week); check opening times on arrival.

musee archeologique de sousse.a: Housed in the kasbah, it contains one of the finest collections of Roman mosaics in Tunisia.
musee archeologique de sousse.c: A must-see in the Sahel for mosaics; best combined with a visit to the kasbah that houses it.
musee archeologique de sousse.d: A museum housed in the Kasbah of Sousse, home to one of the richest collections of Roman mosaics in Tunisia.
musee archeologique de sousse.h: Museum — open during the day (may be closed one day a week); check opening times on site.

musee archeologique et ethnographique de.a: Museum (2007) combining Punic artefacts with collections of folk art and traditions: textiles, jewellery and local crafts.
musee archeologique et ethnographique de.c: A good insight into the material culture of the Sahel; well worth visiting alongside the Moknine synagogue.
musee archeologique et ethnographique de.d: Museum of Punic artefacts and collections of folk art and traditions (textiles, jewellery, crafts). Opened in 2007.
musee archeologique et ethnographique de.h: Museum — open during the day (may be closed one day a week); check opening times on site.

musee d'enfida.a: A former Neo-Romanesque church dating from 1907, converted into a regional museum, displaying a rich collection of Christian funerary mosaics from Uppenna.
musee d'enfida.c: Best visited in conjunction with the nearby site of Uppenna, from which the mosaics originate.
musee d'enfida.d: Former Neo-Romanesque church (1907) converted into a regional museum in 1966. Rich collection of Christian funerary mosaics from Uppenna.
musee d'enfida.h: Museum — open during the day (may be closed one day a week); check opening times on site.

musee dar khadija (hammamet).a: A museum housed in a traditional Hammamet residence, showcasing local architecture and decorative arts.
musee dar khadija (hammamet).c: A short visit to combine with a tour of Hammamet’s medina.
musee dar khadija (hammamet).d: A museum housed in a traditional Hammamet residence.
musee dar khadija (hammamet).h: Museum — open during the day (may be closed one day a week); check opening times on site.

musee de bulla regia.a: Artefacts and mosaics from the Bulla Regia excavations, on display in the on-site museum.
musee de bulla regia.c: Worth visiting alongside the archaeological site; allow about half an hour.
musee de bulla regia.d: Site museum displaying artefacts and mosaics from the excavations at Bulla Regia.
musee de bulla regia.h: Museum — open during the day (may be closed one day a week); check opening times on site.

musee de chemtou.a: The museum dedicated to Numidian yellow marble and the remains of Simitthus, explaining how the quarries were exploited by the Romans.
musee de chemtou.c: Start with the museum to understand the site, then explore the quarries; best combined with a visit to Bulla Regia.
musee de chemtou.d: Archaeological Museum of Numidian Marble and the Ruins of Simitthus (marble quarries).
musee de chemtou.h: Museum — open during the day (may be closed one day a week); check opening times on site.

musee de la memoire commune tuniso-alger.a: The collections dedicated to the shared Tunisian-Algerian history and the struggle for independence, in Ghardimaou.
musee de la memoire commune tuniso-alger.c: Historical themed tour near the border; best combined with a visit to the neighbouring Ain Zana nature reserve.
musee de la memoire commune tuniso-alger.d: Ghardimaou Museum dedicated to the shared Tunisian-Algerian history (the struggle for independence).
musee de la memoire commune tuniso-alger.h: Museum — open during the day (may be closed one day a week); check opening times on site.

musee de mahdia.a: Mahdia Archaeological and Ethnographic Museum (1997), showcasing the history of the city and its region.
musee de mahdia.c: Best combined with a visit to the medina and Borj el-Kebir.
musee de mahdia.d: Mahdia Archaeological and Ethnographic Museum, separate from Borj el-Kebir.
musee de mahdia.h: Museum — open during the day (may be closed one day a week); check opening times on site.

musee de nabeul.a: Archaeological museum showcasing collections from the Cap Bon sites (Neapolis, Kerkouane): mosaics, stelae and Punic and Roman artefacts.
musee de nabeul.c: Ideal for preparing for or extending a visit to Kerkouane and Neapolis.
musee de nabeul.d: Nabeul Archaeological Museum (medina), collections from the Cap Bon sites (Neapolis, Kerkouane): mosaics, stelae and Punic and Roman artefacts.
musee de nabeul.h: Museum — open during the day (may be closed one day a week); check opening times on site.

musee de teboursouk.a: Archaeological collections from the region’s ancient sites, notably Dougga.
musee de teboursouk.c: A short visit to complement your trip to Dougga; check opening times on arrival.
musee de teboursouk.d: Archaeological museum housing collections from the region’s ancient sites, notably Dougga.
musee de teboursouk.h: Museum — open during the day (may be closed one day a week); check opening times on arrival.

musee des arts et traditions populaires.a: Museum of Folk Arts and Traditions located in the medina of Monastir (established in 1985).
musee des arts et traditions populaires.c: A visit to include as part of a tour of Monastir’s medina and ribat.
musee des arts et traditions populaires.d: Monastir Museum of Folk Arts and Traditions, in the medina (established in 1985).
musee des arts et traditions populaires.h: Museum — open during the day (may be closed one day a week); check opening times on site.

musee du patrimoine insulaire de kerkenn.a: A museum dedicated to the heritage and traditions of the Kerkennah Archipelago, particularly fishing.
musee du patrimoine insulaire de kerkenn.c: Well worth a visit to gain an insight into island life before setting off to explore the islands.
musee du patrimoine insulaire de kerkenn.d: Island Heritage Museum on the Kerkennah Archipelago.
musee du patrimoine insulaire de kerkenn.h: Museum — open during the day (may be closed one day a week); check opening times on arrival.

musee du tapis de kairouan.a: A museum dedicated to Kairouan carpets, an iconic craft of the city.
musee du tapis de kairouan.c: A good introduction before visiting the weavers’ workshops in the medina.
musee du tapis de kairouan.d: Museum dedicated to Kairouan carpets, in the medina.
musee du tapis de kairouan.h: Museum — open during the day (may be closed one day a week); opening times to be checked on arrival.

musee national d'art moderne et contempo.a: The collections of modern and contemporary Tunisian paintings and sculptures, on display at the Cité de la Culture.
musee national d'art moderne et contempo.c: A contemporary complement to the Bardo; check the opening days of the Cité de la Culture.
musee national d'art moderne et contempo.d: Museum of Modern and Contemporary Tunisian Art, in the Cité de la Culture in Tunis.
musee national d'art moderne et contempo.h: Museum — open during the day (may be closed one day a week); check opening times on site.

musee national d'utique.a: The Punic and Roman archaeological collections from the site of Utica: artefacts, statues and mosaics.
musee national d'utique.c: Best visited just before or after the nearby site of Utica; allow about 1 hour.
musee national d'utique.d: Archaeological Museum of the Punic and Roman remains at the site of Utica.
musee national d'utique.h: Museum — open during the day (may be closed one day a week); check opening times on site.

musee national de carthage.a: the sarcophagi of Punic priests and priestesses; the stelae from the Tophet; the mosaics and the model of Roman Carthage; the view from Byrsa.
musee national de carthage.c: Best visited at the start of your tour of Carthage to get a sense of the layout of the various sites.
musee national de carthage.d: Archaeological Museum on Byrsa Hill: Punic and Roman collections from the Carthage excavations (stelae, sarcophagi, mosaics).
musee national de carthage.h: Museum — open during the day (may be closed one day a week); check opening times on site.

musee national du bardo.a: The world’s finest collection of Roman mosaics (Virgil, Ulysses and the Sirens, Neptune); the Punic galleries and the artefacts from the Mahdia shipwreck.
musee national du bardo.c: Allow two to three hours; a highlight of any visit to Tunis.
musee national du bardo.d: Tunisia’s main museum, housed in a former Beylical palace in the Bardo. It boasts one of the world’s richest collections of Roman mosaics, as well as Punic, early Christian and Islamic artefacts.
musee national du bardo.h: Museum — open during the day (may be closed one day a week); check opening times on site.

musee oceanographique de bizerte.a: Collections of Mediterranean marine flora and fauna, on display near the old harbour.
musee oceanographique de bizerte.c: A short, sheltered visit, ideal in bad weather; best combined with a stroll around the old harbour.
musee oceanographique de bizerte.d: Museum of Marine Fauna and Flora, near the old port of Bizerte.
musee oceanographique de bizerte.h: Museum — open during the day (may be closed one day a week); check opening times on site.

musee paleochretien de carthage.a: Early Christian remains and artefacts (sarcophagi, mosaics, architectural elements) displayed in a site museum in the heart of Carthage.
musee paleochretien de carthage.c: A short themed stop to include in your tour of Carthage.
musee paleochretien de carthage.d: Site museum showcasing the early Christian remains of Carthage.
musee paleochretien de carthage.h: Museum — open during the day (may be closed one day a week); check opening times on site.

musee regional des arts et traditions du.a: The ethnographic collections on the way of life of Tunisia’s tribes, in the former Sufi zaouïa of Sidi Ben Aissa (1784).
musee regional des arts et traditions du.c: Allow about 1 hour; a good stop to gain an understanding of the local culture before exploring the region.
musee regional des arts et traditions du.d: An ethnographic museum housed in the former zaouïa of Sidi Ben Aissa, a Sufi complex dating from 1784. Opened in 1970, it showcases the way of life of Tunisia’s tribes.
musee regional des arts et traditions du.h: Museum — open during the day (may be closed one day a week); check opening times on site.

musti (mustis).a: The temples, the Arch of Gordian III, the macellum and the ancient oil mills lining the Carthage–Theveste road.
musti (mustis).c: A roadside site that’s easy to explore in about an hour; can be combined with a visit to El Krib.
