musti (mustis).d: A Roman city on the Carthage–Theveste road, featuring temples, the Arch of Gordian III and oil mills. Coordinates of the centre of the site.

naraggara (sakiet sidi youssef).a: The remains of the ancient city mentioned by Livy near Scipio’s camp before Zama, at Sakiet Sidi Youssef.
naraggara (sakiet sidi youssef).c: Near the Algerian border: mainly of historical interest; check for information on access to the border area.
naraggara (sakiet sidi youssef).d: The ancient city of Africa Proconsularis, mentioned by Livy near Scipio’s camp prior to the Battle of Zama (202 BC). Corresponds to Sakiet Sidi Youssef, near the Algerian border.

neapolis (nabeul).a: Ancient garum workshops by the sea and a large house with mosaics, bearing witness to the activity of the coastal city of Neapolis.
neapolis (nabeul).c: An open-air site near the Nabeul seafront, best visited in conjunction with the town’s archaeological museum.
neapolis (nabeul).d: An ancient coastal city near present-day Nabeul, known for its garum production workshops and a large house with mosaics.

nebeur.a: A village near the Mellegue Dam and its wadi landscapes.
nebeur.c: Combine with a visit to the nearby Mellegue Dam.
nebeur.d: A town in the Kef governorate, near the Mellegue Dam.

necropole de haouch taacha.a: Roman necropolis in the south of the Kairouan governorate.
necropole de haouch taacha.c: An inconspicuous site: you’ll need a guide to find it.
necropole de haouch taacha.d: Roman necropolis in the south of the Kairouan governorate.

necropole de kerkouane.a: Punic tombs carved into the rock, serving as a burial complement to the neighbouring city of Kerkouane.
necropole de kerkouane.c: Well worth a visit whilst you’re at the Kerkouane site, to which it is linked.
necropole de kerkouane.d: Rock-cut necropolis associated with the Punic city of Kerkouane, featuring tombs carved into the rock.

nefza.a: The forested and mountainous landscape of the north-west of the Beja governorate, on the edge of the Kroumirie region.
nefza.c: Above all, a nature stop: best combined with a visit to Djebel Khroufa and the surrounding forests in spring.
nefza.d: A town in the north-west of the Beja governorate, a forested and mountainous region close to the Kroumirie.

nouvelle matmata.a: A new town built on the Aradh plateau to resettle the Berber people from the Matmata mountains.
nouvelle matmata.c: A stopover on the way to historic Matmata and its cave dwellings.
nouvelle matmata.d: A new town built on the Aradh plateau to resettle the Berber populations from the Matmata mountains.

numluli (henchir el matria).a: The forum with a capitol, two sets of thermal baths, an early Christian basilica and cisterns, in one of the best-preserved cities in the north, situated between Béja and Dougga.
numluli (henchir el matria).c: A quiet, rural site: make sure you have a car and plenty of water, and combine a visit with Dougga as part of the same trip.
numluli (henchir el matria).d: A Roman city covering approximately 18 ha between Beja and Dougga, one of the best-preserved in the north. Forum with a capitol, two thermal baths, an early Christian basilica and cisterns.

oasis de gafsa.a: Historic oasis system with three-tiered terraced farming, recognised as a Global Important Agricultural Heritage System (GIAHS, 2011).
oasis de gafsa.c: A stroll through the palm grove during the cooler hours of the day; a guide explains the irrigation system.
oasis de gafsa.d: Historic oasis system (~700 ha) on the northern edge of the Sahara (Sakdoud, Ksar, Lela, Gafsa, El Guettar), featuring three-tiered terraced farming. Recognised as a GIAHS in 2011.

oasis de ksar ghilane.a: An isolated oasis on the edge of the Grand Erg Oriental, fed by a thermal spring, the gateway to the Sahara.
oasis de ksar ghilane.c: Access via a track: 4x4 recommended; swimming possible at the spring, and sunsets over the dunes.
oasis de ksar ghilane.d: An isolated oasis on the edge of the Grand Erg Oriental, fed by a hot spring. Gateway to the Saharan desert.

oasis de montagne de chebika.a: A mountain oasis at the foot of Djebel el Negueb, fed by a spring and a waterfall.
oasis de montagne de chebika.c: Path to the waterfall: wear sturdy footwear and visit in the morning before the heat sets in and the tourist groups arrive.
oasis de montagne de chebika.d: A mountain oasis at the foot of Djebel el Negueb, fed by a spring and a waterfall. Coordinates centred on the village.

oasis de montagne de mides.a: An oasis perched on the edge of spectacular canyons, near the Algerian border.
oasis de montagne de mides.c: Approach the canyon viewpoints with caution; the low-angle light enhances the landscape’s beauty.
oasis de montagne de mides.d: A mountain oasis perched on the edge of spectacular canyons, near the Algerian border. Coordinates centred on the village.

oasis de montagne de tamerza.a: Tunisia’s largest mountain oasis, with gorges, waterfalls and the old village abandoned after the floods of 1969.
oasis de montagne de tamerza.c: Make sure you wear sturdy footwear for the gorges; the light and cooler temperatures are best in the morning.
oasis de montagne de tamerza.d: Tunisia’s largest mountain oasis, in the Djerid Mountains, with gorges and waterfalls. An old village abandoned after the floods of 1969.

oasis de nefta.a: The Djerid palm grove, famous for the Corbeille de Nefta, the depression that forms the source of the oasis.
oasis de nefta.c: The viewpoint overlooking the Corbeille offers the finest view; come at sunrise.
oasis de nefta.d: The Djerid palm grove, renowned for the Corbeille de Nefta, the depression that is the source of the palm grove. Coordinates centred on the town.

oasis de tozeur.a: The Great Djerid Palm Grove on the shores of Chott el-Jerid, irrigated by a historic network of seguias.
oasis de tozeur.c: A horse-drawn carriage ride or a walk through the palm grove, preferably in the morning.
oasis de tozeur.d: The Great Djerid Palm Grove on the shores of Chott el-Jerid, irrigated by a historic network of seguias. Coordinates centred on the town.

oasis maritime de gabes.a: A rare coastal oasis overlooking the sea directly; its terraced palm grove is now threatened by urbanisation and pollution.
oasis maritime de gabes.c: A stroll beneath the palm trees during the cooler hours; the condition of the oasis varies from one area to another.
oasis maritime de gabes.d: A rare coastal oasis overlooking the sea directly, in the Gulf of Gabès. A terraced palm grove threatened by urbanisation and pollution. Coordinates centred on the town.

ong jmel / mos espa (decor star wars).a: Abandoned Mos Espa film set in the dunes, near the Ong Jmel rock, shaped like a camel’s neck.
ong jmel / mos espa (decor star wars).c: Access via a track through the sand: a 4x4 is recommended, and visit at sunrise or sunset for the best light.
ong jmel / mos espa (decor star wars).d: Abandoned Star Wars film set near Nefta (Tozeur), the fictional spaceport of Mos Espa, near the Ong Jmel rock, shaped like a camel’s neck.

oudhna (uthina).a: The partially restored amphitheatre; the Capitol and its cisterns; the remains of villas with mosaics.
oudhna (uthina).c: Close to Tunis, ideal for a half-day trip combined with Thuburbo Majus.
oudhna (uthina).d: A Roman colony south of Tunis, featuring an amphitheatre, a capitol, thermal baths and cisterns. An important villa and mosaics.
oudhna (uthina).h: Site managed by the AMVPPC — open during the day; opening hours vary by season, so check on site.

oudhref.a: A town and sub-prefecture north-west of Gabès.
oudhref.c: A stop-off point; little of major tourist interest.
oudhref.d: A town and sub-prefecture of the Gabès governorate, north-west of Gabès.

oued akarit.a: A coastal watercourse north of Gabès, notable for its prehistory and the site of a battle in 1943.
oued akarit.c: Site with no tourist facilities: of mainly historical and natural interest.
oued akarit.d: A coastal watercourse north of Gabès flowing into the gulf, a site of prehistoric significance.

ouled el hadef (medina de tozeur).a: Medieval quarter famous for its clay-brick (toub) façades featuring geometric relief patterns.
ouled el hadef (medina de tozeur).c: Stroll through the shaded alleyways on foot, preferably in the morning or late in the day.
ouled el hadef (medina de tozeur).d: The historic quarter of Tozeur, famous for its clay-brick (toub) architecture featuring geometric relief patterns. Medieval medina.

palais borj baccouche (ariana).a: The former Ariana summer residence of the Bey and its architecture, typical of the country estates of Tunisian dignitaries.
palais borj baccouche (ariana).c: A modest site, sometimes with limited access; a brief stop for enthusiasts of Beylical heritage.
palais borj baccouche (ariana).d: The former Ariana Bey’s residence, an example of the holiday architecture favoured by Tunisian dignitaries.

palais de ksar said.a: The 19th-century Beylical Palace, with its ornate salons and the historic setting where the Treaty of Bardo of 1881 was signed, near the Bardo.
palais de ksar said.c: Best combined with a visit to the neighbouring Bardo Museum; check opening times following restoration work.
palais de ksar said.d: 19th-century Beylical Palace near the Bardo, where the Treaty of the Bardo (1881) was signed.

palais de la mohammedia.a: The romantic ruins of the unfinished palace of Ahmed I Bey, nicknamed the ‘Tunisian Versailles’, whose arcades and sections of wall still stand on the plain.
palais de la mohammedia.c: An evocative, derelict site; wear sturdy shoes and take care whilst walking amongst the ruins.
palais de la mohammedia.d: Ruins of the Beylical Palace of Ahmed I Bey (mid-19th century) in La Mohammedia, nicknamed the ‘Tunisian Versailles’, which remains unfinished.

palais de la rose (manouba).a: The former Beylical summer palace and its reception rooms, which now house the National Military Museum with its collection of weapons, uniforms and equipment.
palais de la rose (manouba).c: Of particular interest to military history enthusiasts; check opening times before visiting.
palais de la rose (manouba).d: Former Beylical palace on the Manouba plain, known as the Palais de la Rose. Home to the National Military Museum of Tunisia.

palais ennejma ezzahra.a: Baron d’Erlanger’s Moorish residence and its terraced gardens; the painted drawing rooms; the Centre for Arabic Music’s collection of musical instruments.
palais ennejma ezzahra.c: In Sidi Bou Said: combine your visit with a concert or enjoy the view of the gulf from the gardens.
palais ennejma ezzahra.d: A palace built in Sidi Bou Said by Baron Rodolphe d’Erlanger (early 20th century) in the Arab-Andalusian style. It houses the Centre for Arab and Mediterranean Music.

palais kobbet el nhas (manouba).a: The palatial pavilion crowned with its characteristic copper dome, a remnant of the Beylical summer residences on the Manouba plain.
palais kobbet el nhas (manouba).c: A small, isolated monument best viewed from the outside whilst passing through Manouba.
palais kobbet el nhas (manouba).d: The palatial pavilion with its copper dome in Manouba, a remnant of the Beylical summer residences.

palais mourad bey (manouba).a: The remains of the former Beylical palace associated with the Mouradids, a testament to the holiday resorts to the west of Tunis.
palais mourad bey (manouba).c: A modest site; best visited in conjunction with the other Beylical residences in the Manouba region.
palais mourad bey (manouba).d: Former Beylical palace in Manouba associated with the Mouradids, a holiday resort area to the west of Tunis.

palais presidentiel de carthage.a: The palace and its enclosed grounds can be glimpsed from the outside; as the official residence of the Head of State, the complex is not open to visitors.
palais presidentiel de carthage.c: Site not open to the public and under surveillance: do not photograph the surroundings; simply a landmark on the coastal road.
palais presidentiel de carthage.d: Official residence of the President of the Republic of Tunisia, situated on the seafront in Carthage. A 20th-century palatial complex set within enclosed grounds.

palais saheb ettabaa.a: The ornate reception rooms and courtyard of the former Beylical Palace of the dignitary Saheb Ettabaa in the Halfaouine district.
palais saheb ettabaa.c: Best visited in conjunction with the Saheb Ettabaa Mosque and the bustling Halfaouine square.
palais saheb ettabaa.d: The Beylical palace in the Halfaouine district, associated with the dignitary Saheb Ettabaa, early 19th century.

palmeraie de douz.a: A vast palm grove of over 500,000 palm trees encircling Douz, the gateway to the Sahara.
palmeraie de douz.c: A shaded stroll through the palm grove; combine it with an excursion to the nearby dunes.
palmeraie de douz.d: A vast palm grove (>500,000 palm trees) encircling Douz, the gateway to the Sahara (Kebili). Coordinates centred on the town.

parc du belvedere.a: The largest park in Tunis on its wooded hill; the Ottoman koubba; the panoramic view of the city and the lake.
parc du belvedere.c: A pleasant morning stroll in the shade of olive and pine trees, in the heart of Tunis.
parc du belvedere.d: Tunis’s largest and oldest urban park (1892), situated on a wooded hill overlooking the city and the lake.

parc ennahli.a: The extensive reforested area on the hills north of Tunis and its panoramic viewpoint over the city and the lake.
parc ennahli.c: A popular spot for Sunday walks and picnics; unobstructed views on clear days.
parc ennahli.d: A vast urban park and reforested area on the hills north of Tunis (Ariana), with a viewpoint overlooking the city.

parc national d'el feija.a: The Kroumirie forest of cork oaks and zeen oaks, a refuge for the Barbary deer.
parc national d'el feija.c: Best visited in spring or autumn for the forest and wildlife; allow for travel by vehicle and walking, and observe the deer at dawn or dusk.
parc national d'el feija.d: Kroumirie National Park, set amongst forests of cork oaks and Zeen oaks. A refuge for the Barbary deer. Approximate coordinates.

parc national de bou hedma.a: A pre-Saharan steppe park and biosphere reserve, home to North Africa’s last acacia savannah and reintroduced antelopes.
parc national de bou hedma.c: Restricted access: check with the park authorities before visiting.
parc national de bou hedma.d: A pre-Saharan steppe national park and biosphere reserve. A site for the reintroduction of antelopes and home to North Africa’s last acacia savannah.

parc national de boukornine.a: Trails through the Mediterranean forest, the flora (cyclamen, irises) and viewpoints overlooking the Gulf of Tunis from the twin-peaked mountain.
parc national de boukornine.c: Ideal in spring for the flora; walking boots, water, and departure from Hammam Lif.
parc national de boukornine.d: National park on Djebel Boukornine, a twin-peaked mountain overlooking the Gulf of Tunis near Hammam Lif. Rich Mediterranean flora.

parc national de chambi.a: The national park, established in 1980 around Djebel Chambi, a UNESCO biosphere reserve and the country’s highest peak.
parc national de chambi.c: Restricted access: check permits and safety arrangements before your visit, and allow a full day.
parc national de chambi.d: A national park established in 1980 around Djebel Chambi, a UNESCO biosphere reserve.

parc national de dghoumes.a: A pre-Saharan steppe park on the edge of Chott el-Jerid, dedicated to wildlife reintroduction.
parc national de dghoumes.c: Wildlife spotting is best early in the morning; find out about access arrangements.
parc national de dghoumes.d: National park on the edge of Chott el-Jerid, at the foot of the djebel. A reserve for pre-Saharan steppe and wildlife reintroduction.

parc national de djebel chambi.a: Tunisia’s highest peak (1,544 m) is situated within an Aleppo pine forest designated as a biosphere reserve, home to mountain wildlife.
parc national de djebel chambi.c: Access is restricted: check for permits and safety requirements, and allow a full day and plenty of water for the hike.
parc national de djebel chambi.d: National park home to Djebel Chambi, Tunisia’s highest peak (1,544 m). A biosphere reserve covering an Aleppo pine forest.

parc national de jbil.a: Tunisia’s largest national park, in the heart of the Grand Erg Oriental, a refuge for gazelles and addax.
parc national de jbil.c: Deep desert: access by 4x4 with an authorised guide; water supplies are compulsory.
parc national de jbil.d: A Saharan national park situated in the Grand Erg Oriental, the largest in Tunisia. A reserve home to gazelles and addax.

parc national de jebel orbata.a: A mountain park near Gafsa, featuring gorges, springs and flora transitional between the Mediterranean and Saharan zones.
parc national de jebel orbata.c: Hiking in rugged terrain: sturdy footwear, water and an early start are essential.
parc national de jebel orbata.d: A mountain national park in the Gafsa region, featuring gorges and springs. Flora transitional between the Mediterranean and Saharan zones.

parc national de jebel serj.a: The Ain Soltane Cave and forests of Aleppo pine and holm oak on the Tunisian Ridge.
parc national de jebel serj.c: A lovely springtime nature walk; make sure you bring good walking shoes and water.
parc national de jebel serj.d: Tunisian Mountain Range National Park, comprising the Ain Soltane cave and forests of Aleppo pine and holm oak.

parc national de jebel zaghouan.a: The trails through the limestone massif, with views over the plain and the Temple of the Waters nestled at its foot.
parc national de jebel zaghouan.c: A cool hike at altitude; make sure you have good walking shoes and plenty of water, and combine it with a visit to the Temple of the Waters.
parc national de jebel zaghouan.d: A national park protecting Mount Zaghouan (1,295 m) and the Temple of the Waters, which supplied Carthage with water. The limestone massif of the Tunisian Ridge.

parc national de l'ichkeul.a: The lake and its wetlands; herds of buffalo; the eco-museum and the trail to the thermal springs at the foot of the djebel; flocks of migratory birds.
parc national de l'ichkeul.c: Visit in winter to see waterbirds (coots, geese, flamingos); binoculars recommended.
parc national de l'ichkeul.d: The national park around Lake Ichkeul and its wetlands, a UNESCO World Heritage Site and a Ramsar site. A major stopover for migratory birds.

parc national de oued zen.a: The Kroumirie oak forest and the Barbary deer it protects, south of Tabarka.
parc national de oued zen.c: Best visited in spring or autumn; you’ll need a vehicle and to walk to reach the forest.
parc national de oued zen.d: Kroumirie National Park, protecting the Zen oak forest and the Barbary deer, south of Tabarka.

parc national de sidi toui.a: A desert steppe park in the south-east, dedicated to the rehabilitation of Saharan wildlife.
parc national de sidi toui.c: Remote area near the border: a guide and 4x4 are recommended.
parc national de sidi toui.d: A desert steppe national park in south-eastern Tunisia, near the Libyan border. A reserve for the rehabilitation of Saharan wildlife.

parc national des iles de zembra et zemb.a: Marine and Island Park off Cap Bon, a UNESCO Biosphere Reserve and an important seabird breeding site.
parc national des iles de zembra et zemb.c: Access is restricted; consider a guided boat trip rather than disembarking independently.
parc national des iles de zembra et zemb.d: Marine and Island National Park off Cap Bon, a UNESCO biosphere reserve. An important seabird breeding site. Approximate coordinates.

petite mosquee de beja.a: A historic mosque, more modest than the Great Mosque, in the heart of the medina of Beja.
petite mosquee de beja.c: Well worth a look whilst strolling through the medina; smart dress is required.
petite mosquee de beja.d: The historic mosque in the medina of Beja, more modest than the Great Mosque.

phare de chebba.a: Lighthouse near Cape Ras Kapoudia, on the rocky Sahel coastline.
phare de chebba.c: Coastal viewpoint: approach via the coast, as access to the lighthouse itself may be restricted.
phare de chebba.d: Chebba Lighthouse, near Cape Ras Kapoudia.

phare de l'ile charki (kerkennah).a: The lighthouse on Charki Island, at the entrance to the Sfax channel, in the Kerkennah archipelago.
phare de l'ile charki (kerkennah).c: Visible during a boat trip around the archipelago.
phare de l'ile charki (kerkennah).d: Lighthouse on Charki Island (Kerkennah), at the entrance to the Sfax channel.

phare de mahdia (cap afrique).a: Lighthouse at the tip of the peninsula (Cap Afrique), a maritime landmark offering views of the coastline.
phare de mahdia (cap afrique).c: A lovely walk to the tip; access to the interior may be restricted.
phare de mahdia (cap afrique).d: Lighthouse at the tip of the Mahdia peninsula (Cap Afrique).

phare de ras thyna.a: Lighthouse at Cape Ras Thyna, south of Sfax, near the ancient site of Thaenae.
phare de ras thyna.c: Coastal landmark to be approached from the coast; to be used in conjunction with the site of Thyna.
phare de ras thyna.d: Lighthouse at Cape Ras Thyna, south of Sfax.

phare du cap angela.a: The lighthouse marking Cape Angela (Ras ben Sakka), the northernmost point of mainland Africa.
phare du cap angela.c: A landmark marking the tip of the continent; combine your visit with Cape Angela and Cape Blanc.
phare du cap angela.d: Lighthouse marking Cape Angela (Ras ben Sakka), the northernmost point of mainland Africa.

pheradi maius (sidi khalifa).a: A well-preserved Roman city near Sidi Khalifa: temples, thermal baths, a triumphal arch, a forum and the remains of an amphitheatre.
pheradi maius (sidi khalifa).c: An open-air site off the beaten track; enquire locally about access.
pheradi maius (sidi khalifa).d: A Roman city in Proconsular Africa near Sidi Khalifa, north of Enfidha. Temples, thermal baths, a triumphal arch, a forum and an amphitheatre.

piscines romaines de gafsa.a: Two open-air Roman basins fed by springs, with Latin inscriptions, in the heart of the medina.
piscines romaines de gafsa.c: A short visit, with some shade at times; combine it with the nearby museum and mosque.
piscines romaines de gafsa.d: Roman pools fed by springs in the heart of the medina of Gafsa, the ancient Capsa. Two central open-air pools, bearing Latin inscriptions.

place de la kasbah.a: The Almohad minaret of the Kasbah Mosque; the harmony of the official square; the view towards the Upper Medina.
place de la kasbah.c: Not open to visitors (seat of government), but very photogenic from the outside. A natural gateway to the Upper Medina.
place de la kasbah.d: A vast administrative square to the west of the medina, the heart of Tunisian power: the Prime Minister’s Office (Dar El Bey) and government buildings, the Kasbah Mosque and its Almohad minaret. The official buildings are not open to visitors, but the complex as a whole — square, palace and mosque — is well worth a look.

place halfaouine.a: The bustling square and its souks; the nearby Saheb Ettabaa Mosque; the hammam made famous by the film.
place halfaouine.c: The heart of the working-class north – take a stroll, have a coffee. More authentic and less touristy than the centre.
place halfaouine.d: A lively square in the northern part of the medina, bustling with two souks (El Halfaouine and El Jedid). On the edge of the square stands the Youssef Saheb Ettabaa Mosque (1814). Its hammam inspired the cult film ‘Halfaouine, l’enfant des terrasses’ (Férid Boughedir, 1990, winner of the Tanit d’Or at the JCC), which brought the neighbourhood’s atmosphere to the attention of the whole world.

plage de chaffar.a: Beach on the Gulf of Gabès, south of Sfax.
plage de chaffar.c: A place for swimming and relaxation; check conditions on site.
plage de chaffar.d: Beach on the coast of the Gulf of Gabès, south of Sfax.

plaine de gammouda.a: Agricultural plain in the central part of the governorate of Sidi Bouzid.
plaine de gammouda.c: Rural landscape rather than a tourist site: to be passed through along the road.
plaine de gammouda.d: The Gammouda agricultural plain, in the central part of the governorate of Sidi Bouzid.

pont de medjez el-bab.a: The Ottoman bridge with eight arches over the Medjerda, completed in 1677 under Mourad II Bey, featuring reused Roman stones; still in use.
pont de medjez el-bab.c: Visible from the riverbanks; a brief stop along the way, to be combined with a visit to the nearby Medjez el-Bab memorial.
pont de medjez el-bab.d: An eight-arched bridge over the Medjerda, completed in 1677 under Mourad II Bey, featuring reused Roman stones. Still in use.

pont de trajan (chemtou).a: The remains of the Roman bridge spanning the Medjerda wadi, linked to the transport of marble from Chemtou.
pont de trajan (chemtou).c: A brief stop as part of the tour of the Chemtou site; the water level of the wadi is lower and the crossing is easier outside the rainy season.
pont de trajan (chemtou).d: Roman bridge spanning the Medjerda wadi near Simitthus, linked to the quarrying and transport of Chemtou marble.

pont mobile de bizerte.a: The bascule bridge, built in 1980, spanning the Bizerte Canal and linking the city to Zarzouna, is an iconic feature of the urban landscape.
pont mobile de bizerte.c: A sight worth seeing from the quays, particularly when the bridge is raised to allow ships to pass.
pont mobile de bizerte.d: The iconic bascule bridge spanning the Bizerte Canal, linking the city to Zarzouna.

pont romain sur l'oued djilf.a: Roman bridge spanning the Djilf wadi, in the Oueslatia region.
pont romain sur l'oued djilf.c: A quick stop for lovers of Roman architecture, by car.
pont romain sur l'oued djilf.d: Roman bridge spanning the Djilf wadi, in the Oueslatia region.

pont-aqueduc sur l'oued cherchira.a: Ancient hydraulic structure spanning the Cherchira wadi, near Haffouz.
pont-aqueduc sur l'oued cherchira.c: Worth a look if you’re travelling through the Haffouz region.
pont-aqueduc sur l'oued cherchira.d: Ancient aqueduct bridge spanning the Cherchira wadi, near Haffouz.

pont-barrage d'el batan.a: The ancient waterworks on the Medjerda and the remains of the fulling mills that made the valley’s reputation for textiles.
pont-barrage d'el batan.c: An interesting example of historic industrial heritage, well worth seeing on a tour of the Medjerda Valley.
pont-barrage d'el batan.d: An ancient hydraulic structure on the Medjerda at El Batan, linked to the fulling mills of the valley.

ports puniques de carthage.a: the circular Admiralty islet and the water area of the military harbour; the rectangular merchant harbour; the scale model at the small Antiquarium museum.
ports puniques de carthage.c: A quick site to visit, best combined with the nearby Tophet.
ports puniques de carthage.d: The two ancient harbours of Carthage: a rectangular merchant harbour and a circular military harbour (the Admiralty Harbour). Remains still visible in the present-day landscape.
ports puniques de carthage.h: Site managed by the AMVPPC — open during the day; opening hours vary according to the season, so check on site.

pupput.a: Remains of a Roman coastal town near Hammamet: necropolis and mosaics in domestic buildings.
pupput.c: A modest, out-of-the-way site in the southern Hammamet hotel zone; a quick visit to combine with the Hammamet medina.
pupput.d: Roman city on the coast near Hammamet, known for its necropolis and house mosaics.
pupput.h: Site managed by the AMVPPC — open during the day; opening hours vary depending on the season, so please check on site.

quartier hannibal (carthage).a: The streets and foundations of Punic dwellings unearthed on the southern slope of Byrsa, bearing witness to the urban layout of Carthage prior to 146 BC.
quartier hannibal (carthage).c: Well worth a visit immediately after the Byrsa Museum to understand the original Punic city.
quartier hannibal (carthage).d: Remains of a Punic residential quarter on the southern slope of Byrsa, illustrating the urban layout of Carthage prior to 146 BC.

quartier magon.a: The remains of Punic dwellings excavated by the sea and the small open-air site museum explaining the urban layout of Carthage.
quartier magon.c: A short walk along the coast, to be combined with a visit to the nearby Baths of Antoninus.
quartier magon.d: A Punic residential quarter of Carthage, excavated by the sea, featuring the remains of dwellings and an open-air site museum. Approximate coordinates.

raf raf.a: The large beach facing Pilau Island and the coastal town’s Andalusian heritage.
raf raf.c: Primarily a seaside destination: best visited in the warmer months and combined with a visit to the nearby Cape Sidi Ali El Mekki.
raf raf.d: A coastal town famous for its beach and its Andalusian heritage, facing Pilau Island.

raqqada.a: Former Aghlabid princely capital south of Kairouan, now best known for its National Museum of Islamic Art (Kairouan Qur’anic manuscripts).
raqqada.c: Site some distance from the centre: combine this visit with a trip to Kairouan by car.
raqqada.d: Former princely residence and Aghlabid capital south of Kairouan. Site of the National Museum of Islamic Art.

ras djezira (chebba).a: Coastal headland in the south of the Mahdia governorate, near Chebba.
ras djezira (chebba).c: A pleasant seaside viewpoint; wear sturdy footwear on the rocks.
ras djezira (chebba).d: Coastal headland in the south of the governorate, near Chebba.

ras salakta.a: Salakta headland, near the ancient site of the same name.
ras salakta.c: Best combined with a visit to the Salakta site and museum.

redeyef.a: A phosphate mining town in the Gafsa Basin, the epicentre of the 2008 social movement.
redeyef.c: Of mainly historical and social interest; a stop on the Lezard Rouge line.
redeyef.d: A phosphate mining town in the Gafsa Basin, the epicentre of the 2008 social movement.

remada (tillibari).a: A southern town on the site of the ancient Roman fort of Tillibari (Limes), near the Libyan border.
remada (tillibari).c: Remote border area: check access details and carry plenty of water with you.
remada (tillibari).d: A southern town near the Libyan border, on the site of the ancient Roman fort of Tillibari (limes).

remparts de monastir.a: The ancient walls of the Monastir medina, separate from the ribat, marking the historic layout of the town.
remparts de monastir.c: To be explored whilst walking through the medina during a visit to the ribat.
remparts de monastir.d: The ancient walls of Monastir’s medina, separate from the ribat.

reserve naturelle d'ain zana.a: The oak woodland and forest biodiversity of Kroumirie, near Ghardimaou.
reserve naturelle d'ain zana.c: A nature stop to combine with Ghardimaou and El Feija Park; best visited in spring.
reserve naturelle d'ain zana.d: Kroumirie Nature Reserve near Ghardimaou, with its oak stands and forest biodiversity.

reserve naturelle d'el gonna.a: Nature reserve and protected area in the governorate of Sfax.
reserve naturelle d'el gonna.c: Access to the reserve: check the conditions before visiting.
reserve naturelle d'el gonna.d: Nature reserve and protected area in the governorate of Sfax.

reserve naturelle djebel rihana-djebel g.a: Nature reserve of approximately 2,000 ha covering the Rihana and Goulebe djebels, in the Souk Jedid district.
reserve naturelle djebel rihana-djebel g.c: Access to the reserve: check the conditions before visiting.
reserve naturelle djebel rihana-djebel g.d: Nature reserve (~2,000 ha) covering the Djebels Rihana and Goulebe, Souk Jedid district.

ribat de lamta.a: Small Aghlabid ribat dating from 859 in Lamta (Leptis Minor): a square, single-storey building with rounded corner towers and a courtyard featuring an underground cistern.
ribat de lamta.c: To be visited in conjunction with the nearby Lamta Archaeological Museum.
ribat de lamta.d: Small Aghlabid ribat at Lamta (Leptis Minor), built in 859. A single-storey square building with rounded corner towers and a courtyard containing an underground cistern.

ribat de monastir.a: A labyrinth of courtyards, rooms and staircases; the panoramic watchtower; the Museum of Islamic Art housed within the complex.
ribat de monastir.c: A setting for famous films; climb the tower for views of the sea and the Bourguiba mausoleum.
ribat de monastir.d: The Ribat of Monastir, one of the oldest Islamic defensive structures in Ifriqiya (founded around 796), expanded over the centuries.
ribat de monastir.h: Site managed by the AMVPPC — open during the day; opening hours vary by season, so check on site.

ribat de sousse.a: The fortified courtyard and the cells of the monk-soldiers; the oratory; the watchtower (nador) offering a panoramic view of the medina.
ribat de sousse.c: Climb the narrow tower early in the morning to catch the light and avoid the crowds.
ribat de sousse.d: The Ribat (fortified monastery) of Sousse, built during the Aghlabid period (8th–9th centuries), with its watchtower (nador) overlooking the medina.
ribat de sousse.h: Site managed by the AMVPPC — open during the day; opening hours vary according to the season, so check on site.

rougga (bararus).a: The ancient Roman city of Bararus, about ten kilometres south-east of El Jem.
rougga (bararus).c: A largely undeveloped rural site: a guide helps visitors to locate and interpret it.
rougga (bararus).d: The ancient Roman city of Bararus, approximately 13 km south-east of El Jem.

rouhia.a: A town in the cereal-growing highlands of southern Siliana.
rouhia.c: A simple stopover in an agricultural area.
rouhia.d: A town in the south of the governorate of Siliana, in the highland grain-growing region.

ruspina.a: An ancient Punic and later Roman city corresponding to present-day Monastir, mentioned in ancient sources (Caesar’s Civil War); very few remains.
ruspina.c: More of a historical landmark than a site open to visitors, as the modern city has built over the ancient one.
ruspina.d: Ancient Punic and later Roman city corresponding to present-day Monastir, mentioned in ancient sources (Caesar’s Civil War).

sabria.a: An oasis village nestled amongst the first major dunes, about thirty kilometres from Douz.
sabria.c: Saharan setting: come and admire the dunes in the low light of morning or evening.
sabria.d: Oasis village in the Kebili governorate, nestled amongst the first major dunes, around 30 km from Douz.

salakta (sullecthum).a: Ancient Roman port of the Sahel, a centre for the production of oil and garum: coastal ruins and a small local museum (lion mosaic).
salakta (sullecthum).c: Combine a visit to the site and its museum with a stroll along the seafront.
salakta (sullecthum).d: Ancient Roman port of the Sahel (Sullecthum), a centre for the production and export of oil and garum. Small museum and coastal ruins.

sanctuaire de thinissut.a: Punic-Roman sanctuary dedicated to Baal Hammon and Tanit, at Bir Bou Rekba near Hammamet; its terracotta statues are housed in the Bardo Museum.
sanctuaire de thinissut.c: On site, the remains are sparse; the main statues can be seen at the Bardo in Tunis.
sanctuaire de thinissut.d: Punic-Roman sanctuary dedicated to Baal Hammon and Tanit, at Bir Bou Rekba near Hammamet. Terracotta statues at the Bardo.

sbeitla (sufetula).a: The Sufetula forum, with its paved floor, opens onto three adjoining Capitoline temples dedicated to the Triad, the Arch of Antoninus Pius and several Christian basilicas with baptisteries.
sbeitla (sufetula).c: Allow 2 to 3 hours for your visit and make the most of the low-angle light in the morning or late afternoon to photograph the Capitoline temples.
sbeitla (sufetula).d: An ancient Roman and Byzantine city notable for its forum and its three adjoining Capitoline temples, as well as its Christian basilicas.
sbeitla (sufetula).h: Site managed by the AMVPPC — open during the day; opening hours vary according to the season, so please check on site.

sbiba (ville).a: The town stands on the site of ancient Sufes, whose basilica has been converted into a mosque.
sbiba (ville).c: Look out for the ruins of Sufes scattered throughout the town; a short visit.
sbiba (ville).d: A town in the governorate of Kasserine, situated on the site of ancient Sufes (where the basilica has been converted into a mosque).

sebkha ben ghiadha.c: Wetland best viewed from the surrounding area; binoculars recommended.

sebkha cherita.a: Sebkha in the west of the Mahdia governorate.
sebkha cherita.c: Naturalist’s interest: observe waterbirds without venturing onto the salt flats.
sebkha cherita.d: Sebkha in the west of the Mahdia governorate.

sebkha de kelbia.a: An intermittent salt lake (~8,000 ha) north of Kairouan, a nature reserve and a major wetland for waterbirds after Ichkeul.
sebkha de kelbia.c: Of particular interest to birdwatchers after the rains, when the lake is full; binoculars recommended.
sebkha de kelbia.d: An intermittent salt lake (~8,000 ha) in the Kairouan plain, north of the city. The second-largest wetland after Ichkeul, a nature reserve since 1993. Approximate coordinates.

sebkha de moknine.a: A salt depression south-east of Moknine, a wetland of interest for birdlife.
sebkha de moknine.c: Of ornithological interest; worth combining with a visit to Moknine.
sebkha de moknine.d: A salt depression south-east of Moknine, a wetland of interest for birdlife.

sebkha de rades.a: The peri-urban salt marsh on the southern edge of Lake Tunis, frequented by waterbirds.
sebkha de rades.c: Wetland in an urbanised area: observation from the surrounding area; of particular ornithological interest in winter.
sebkha de rades.d: A salt marsh on the southern edge of Lake Tunis, near Rades, a peri-urban wetland.

sebkha de sidi el hani (sousse).a: Large salt lake (~36,000 ha) south-west of Sousse, a salt flat subject to periodic flooding.
sebkha de sidi el hani (sousse).c: A salt landscape that changes with the seasons; an undeveloped natural site.
sebkha de sidi el hani (sousse).d: Large salt lake (~36,000 ha) south-west of Sousse. A salt flat subject to periodic flooding.

sebkha el ghorra.a: Temporary salt lake (sebkha) in the west of the Mahdia governorate.
sebkha el ghorra.c: A wetland best viewed from a distance, particularly during the wet season.
sebkha el ghorra.d: Sebkha (temporary salt lake) to the west of the Mahdia governorate.

sebkha el jem.a: Salt flat (sebkha) in the north of the Sfax governorate, near El Jem.
sebkha el jem.c: A wetland best observed from a distance, particularly during the wet season.
sebkha el jem.d: Salt flat (sebkha) in the north of the Sfax Governorate, near El Jem.

sebkha el maamourah.a: Coastal wetland to the south-east of Cap Bon.
sebkha el maamourah.c: A modest natural site, mainly for observing waterbirds.
sebkha el maamourah.d: Sebkha El Maâmourah, a coastal wetland to the south-east of Cap Bon.

sebkha kourzia.a: The large seasonal sebkha in western Zaghouan (El Fahs region) with its salt flats and marshes, depending on the season.
sebkha kourzia.c: Best viewed after rainfall when it is flooded; birdwatching from the surrounding area.
sebkha kourzia.d: Large sebkha in the west of the Zaghouan governorate (El Fahs region), a seasonal wetland.

sebkha tazerka.a: Wetland on the east coast of Cap Bon.
sebkha tazerka.c: An unassuming birding spot; few facilities on site.
sebkha tazerka.d: Sebkha Tazerka, a wetland on the east coast of Cap Bon.

sebkha tsaacha.a: Salt flat (sebkha) in the south of the Kairouan governorate.
sebkha tsaacha.c: A wetland best viewed from a distance; avoid venturing onto the salt crust.
sebkha tsaacha.d: Sebkha (salt flat) in the south of the Kairouan governorate.

sebkhet ariana.a: The brackish lagoon north of Tunis and its birdlife, notably flamingos and waterbirds.
sebkhet ariana.c: Birdwatching from the surrounding area; good light at dawn, binoculars recommended.
sebkhet ariana.d: A brackish lagoon north of Tunis, separated from the sea by a sand dune ridge. A wetland home to flamingos and waterbirds.

sebkhet el melah de zarzis.a: Vast salt sebkha (~150 km²) near Zarzis, separated from the sea by a dune ridge and used for salt production.
sebkhet el melah de zarzis.c: Photogenic reflections in low-angle light; stay on the accessible paths.
sebkhet el melah de zarzis.d: Vast salt sebkha near Zarzis (~150 km²), separated from the sea by a dune ridge, exploited for salt.

sebkhet en noual.a: A vast salt depression in the central steppe (~17,000 ha), a Ramsar wetland on the border between Sidi Bouzid and Sfax, frequented by waterbirds.
sebkhet en noual.c: Ornithological interest: binoculars are useful, and avoid walking on the salt crusts.
sebkhet en noual.d: Vast salt depression in the central steppe (~17,000 ha), on the border between Sidi Bouzid and Sfax. A Ramsar wetland since 2007.

sebkhet halk el menzel.a: Coastal salt lagoon (~1,450 ha) near Sidi Khelifa, a Ramsar wetland of international importance for birdlife.
sebkhet halk el menzel.c: Undeveloped natural site; approach with discretion whilst observing birds.
sebkhet halk el menzel.d: Coastal salt lagoon in the governorate of Sousse, near Sidi Khelifa. Ramsar wetland (~1,450 ha), important for birdlife. Approximate coordinates.

sebkhet sejoumi.a: The vast salt depression south-west of Tunis, flooded in winter, frequented by numerous waterbirds.
sebkhet sejoumi.c: Best visited in winter when it is flooded; birdwatching from the surrounding area, avoiding degraded urbanised zones.
sebkhet sejoumi.d: A vast salt pan to the south-west of Tunis, filled with water in winter. An important wetland for birdlife, threatened by urbanisation.

sebkhet soliman.a: Cap Bon wetland designated as a Ramsar site, important for waterbirds.
sebkhet soliman.c: Of primarily ornithological interest; observe from a distance so as not to disturb the birds.
sebkhet soliman.d: Soliman Sebkha, a wetland in Cap Bon and a Ramsar site of importance for waterbirds.

second amphitheatre d'el jem.a: Levelled remains of a second amphitheatre at Thysdrus, older and far less well-preserved than the main amphitheatre.
second amphitheatre d'el jem.c: Worth seeing as a complement to the main amphitheatre, for those who are curious.
second amphitheatre d'el jem.d: Ruins of a second Roman amphitheatre at Thysdrus, distinct from the main amphitheatre.

sedouikech (djerba).a: A village in central Djerba, one of the few places where the island’s Berber culture still survives.
sedouikech (djerba).c: A peaceful retreat in the heart of the island, far from the hustle and bustle of the seaside resorts.
sedouikech (djerba).d: A village in central Djerba, one of the few places where the Djerba Berber language is still spoken.

segermes (henchir harat).a: The remains of the ancient Roman city of Segermes, unearthed by Danish-Tunisian excavations, to the east of the governorate.
segermes (henchir harat).c: A site of scientific interest with few signposts; check locally before visiting.
segermes (henchir harat).d: Site of the ancient Roman city of Segermes, to the east of the governorate of Zaghouan, the subject of Danish-Tunisian excavations.

sejnane.a: The craft of hand-modelled pottery by local women, inscribed on the UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage list in 2018, and the town’s rural atmosphere.
sejnane.c: Look out for potters and cooperatives to view and buy traditional ceramics; best combined with a visit to the nearby wetlands.
sejnane.d: A rural town known for its pottery, hand-modelled by women, inscribed on the UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage list in 2018.

sened.a: A village about 50 km east of Gafsa, known for its ancient Berber dialect.
sened.c: A peaceful stopover; of interest mainly for its culture and language.
sened.d: A village and the administrative centre of the delegation, situated about 50 km east of Gafsa, known for its ancient Berber dialect.

sicca veneria (le kef antique).a: Ancient remains visible beneath the modern town, notably the Roman cisterns and traces of the sanctuary of Venus.
sicca veneria (le kef antique).c: Explore these by strolling through the medina of El Kef, which lies over the ancient city.
sicca veneria (le kef antique).d: An ancient Numidian and later Roman city situated beneath the present-day town of Le Kef, known for its sanctuary and ancient cisterns.

sidi aich.a: A town north of Gafsa, in a region of rugged terrain and mountain oases.
sidi aich.c: Possible starting point for trips to the surrounding mountain oases.
sidi aich.d: A town and the administrative centre of the Gafsa Governorate, situated to the north of Gafsa, in a region of mountainous terrain and mountain oases.

sidi bou said.a: the Café des Nattes at the top of the main street; the blue doors and mashrabiya screens; Baron d’Erlanger’s Ennejma Ezzahra Palace (Museum of Music); the lighthouse and the viewpoint overlooking the gulf; the small marina below.
sidi bou said.c: Come in the late afternoon for the light and the sunset; a pine nut tea at the Café des Délices is a must.
sidi bou said.d: A village perched above the Gulf of Tunis, famous for its white houses with blue doors. A listed site of Andalusian inspiration, situated near Carthage.

siliana (ville).a: The governorate capital, a starting point for visits to ancient sites and the mountains of the Tunisian mountain range.
siliana (ville).c: A good logistical base from which to explore Makthar, Ksar Lemsa and Djebel Serj.
siliana (ville).d: Capital of the governorate of Siliana, on the western edge of the Tunisian mountain range.

site archeologique de thala.a: The necropolis, a two-storey mausoleum and Byzantine fortifications, in a rare town that has retained its ancient name and is associated with Jugurtha.
site archeologique de thala.c: At an altitude of around 1,000 metres: make sure you bring warm clothing, as the site is one of the coldest in Tunisia.
site archeologique de thala.d: A rare town that has retained its ancient name, situated at an altitude of around 1,000 metres, associated with Jugurtha. Necropolis, a two-storey mausoleum and Byzantine fortifications.

skifa kahla (bab zouila).a: The monumental fortified gateway, a remnant of the Fatimid ramparts; the long vaulted passageway leading into the medina of Mahdia.
skifa kahla (bab zouila).c: An ideal starting point for exploring the Mahdia peninsula.
skifa kahla (bab zouila).d: The monumental fortified gate of the medina of Mahdia, a remnant of the Fatimid ramparts erected from 916 onwards. The only land access to the historic peninsula.

souk lahad.a: An oasis town in the Nefzaoua region on the edge of the Chott el-Jerid, about fifteen km from Kebili.
souk lahad.c: Oasis stopover; combine with a crossing of the chott.
souk lahad.d: Oasis town and administrative centre of the Nefzaoua district, situated ~15 km north-west of Kebili, on the edge of the Chott el-Jerid.

sources thermales de korbous.a: The spa resort nestled in a coastal gorge; the Ain Atrous hot spring which flows into the sea.
sources thermales de korbous.c: Swimming is possible where the hot water meets the sea; a scenic road runs along the Cap Bon coastline.
sources thermales de korbous.d: The Cap Bon spa resort, nestled in a coastal gorge, is fed by hot springs, including the Ain Atrous, which flows into the sea. Coordinates centred on the town.

sufes (sbiba).a: The basilica converted into a mosque, the temple, the thermal baths and Justinian’s Byzantine fort, on the site of present-day Sbiba.
sufes (sbiba).c: Ruins scattered throughout the modern town: a short visit to combine with Sbeitla.
sufes (sbiba).d: The Roman city of Byzacene (Colonia Aurelia Sufetana), on the site of present-day Sbiba. A basilica converted into a mosque, a temple, thermal baths and a Byzantine fort built by Justinian.

synagogue beit mordekhai de la goulette.a: The synagogue at La Goulette, a testament to the port’s former Jewish community and its cosmopolitan past.
synagogue beit mordekhai de la goulette.c: Access may be restricted; worth seeing whilst strolling through the La Goulette neighbourhood.
synagogue beit mordekhai de la goulette.d: The synagogue at La Goulette, a testament to the Jewish community of the port of Tunis.

synagogue de la ghriba (djerba).a: The oldest synagogue in Tunisia, in Erriadh, with an interior lined with faience tiles and the site of an annual Jewish pilgrimage.
synagogue de la ghriba (djerba).c: Appropriate attire is required; visitor numbers peak during the spring pilgrimage (Lag Ba’omer).
synagogue de la ghriba (djerba).d: The oldest synagogue in Tunisia, in Erriadh (Hara Seghira) on the island of Djerba, a site of annual Jewish pilgrimage.

synagogue de la ghriba du kef.a: The former Sephardic synagogue in the Jewish quarter of La Hara, restored and reopened in 1994.
synagogue de la ghriba du kef.c: A small building worth seeing whilst strolling through the medina; access is sometimes subject to local authorisation.
synagogue de la ghriba du kef.d: Former synagogue in the Jewish quarter of La Hara, known as Ghribet el Kef, of Sephardic rite. Abandoned in 1984, then restored and reopened in 1994.

synagogue de moknine.a: Former synagogue of the Jewish community of Moknine, a testament to the Jewish-Tunisian heritage of the Sahel.
synagogue de moknine.c: Check locally for visiting arrangements, as the building is not always open.
synagogue de moknine.d: The former synagogue of the Jewish community of Moknine, a testament to Tunisia’s Jewish heritage.

table de jugurtha.a: A spectacular mesa (1,271 m) accessible via a staircase carved into the rock, featuring granaries and cave dwellings, and offering sweeping panoramic views (UNESCO Tentative List).
table de jugurtha.c: Set off in the morning on a clear day; allow 2 to 3 hours for the round trip from Kalaat es Senam, and take water and a hat with you.
table de jugurtha.d: Spectacular mesa (1,271 m) near Kalaat es Senam (Le Kef), a historic refuge attributed to Jugurtha. Granaries and cave dwellings; UNESCO tentative list.

tajerouine.a: A stopover town at the foot of Djebel Slata, a starting point for exploring the surrounding sites.
tajerouine.c: More of a stopover than a destination: useful for exploring the south-west of El Kef.
tajerouine.d: A town in the Kef Governorate, approximately 38 km south-west of Kef, at the foot of Djebel Slata.

takrouna.a: The old white village perched on its rocky outcrop; the zaouïa at the summit; the 360° view over the Sahel plain.
takrouna.c: Climb to the top for the panoramic view; there’s a café overlooking the village.
takrouna.d: A Berber village perched on a rocky outcrop near Enfidha, with its ancient whitewashed buildings. Approximate coordinates of the village summit.

tamezret.a: A Berber village on the slopes of one of the highest peaks of the Matmata Mountains, home to an Amazigh-speaking community (Chelha).
tamezret.c: Panoramic view of the mountains: climb up to the upper village for the view; bring water with you.
tamezret.d: A Berber village on the slopes of one of the highest peaks of the Matmata Mountains (~480 m), about 40 km south-west of Gabès. An Amazigh-speaking community (Chelha).

taoujout.a: A Berber village in the Matmata Mountains, near Tamezret and Zraoua, with an Amazigh-speaking tradition (Chelha).
taoujout.c: Best combined with a visit to Tamezret; the mountain road requires careful driving.
taoujout.d: A Berber village in the Matmata Mountains (Gabès), near Tamezret and Zraoua, where the Chelha Amazigh dialect is traditionally spoken.

tataouine (foum tataouine).a: A former garrison town during the Protectorate, and the gateway to the ksour of the Dahar.
tataouine (foum tataouine).c: Starting point for tours to the ksours: make sure you have plenty of water and fuel.
tataouine (foum tataouine).d: Capital of the Tataouine governorate, a former garrison town of the Protectorate, and gateway to the ksour of Dahar.

tebourba (thuburbo minus).a: The old Andalusian town in the Medjerda Valley and the remains of ancient Thuburbo Minus, including the ruins of the amphitheatre.
tebourba (thuburbo minus).c: A countryside stop in the Medjerda Valley; combine with a visit to the amphitheatre and the Sidi Ali Azouz mausoleum.
tebourba (thuburbo minus).d: A town in the Medjerda Valley on the site of ancient Thuburbo Minus (a Roman colony), repopulated by Andalusians in the 17th century.

teboursouk.a: The historic town of ancient Thubursicum Bure: medina, kasbah and ramparts, gateway to Dougga.
teboursouk.c: A convenient stopover before or after Dougga; make it a stop for amenities and to explore the medina.
teboursouk.d: The historic town of ancient Thubursicum Bure (medina, kasbah, ramparts), gateway to Dougga.

telmine.a: A village on the edge of the Chott el-Jerid, close to the ancient site of Turris Tamalleni.
telmine.c: Best combined with a visit to the nearby ruins of Turris Tamalleni.
telmine.d: The village of Kebili Nord on the edge of the Chott el-Jerid, near the ancient site of Turris Tamalleni.

temple capitolin de tubernuc.a: Ancient Capitoline temple known locally as the ‘Great Monument with Three Doors’, in the Soliman/Grombalia region.
temple capitolin de tubernuc.c: A remote and largely undeveloped site; ask for directions on site to find it.
temple capitolin de tubernuc.d: Ancient Capitoline temple at Tubernuc (Soliman/Grombalia region), known locally as the great Byzantine monument with three gates.

temple d'apollon (bulla regia).a: The remains of the temple dedicated to Apollo, whose statues are now housed in the Bardo Museum.
temple d'apollon (bulla regia).c: A stop on the Bulla Regia tour; to see the statues, extend your visit to the Bardo Museum in Tunis.
temple d'apollon (bulla regia).d: Roman temple dedicated to Apollo at Bulla Regia; the statues are now in the Bardo Museum.

temple des eaux de zaghouan.a: The Roman nymphaeum, shaped like a semicircle and nestled against the side of the djebel, with its basin and niches that collected the springs feeding the Carthage aqueduct, set in wooded surroundings.
temple des eaux de zaghouan.c: Above the town of Zaghouan; a lovely, cool spot to stop off at, to be combined with a hike up to the national park.
temple des eaux de zaghouan.d: A monumental nymphaeum built at the foot of Djebel Zaghouan, capturing the springs that fed the Carthage aqueduct.

thacia.a: The ruins of a Roman city and former bishopric, near El Krib.
thacia.c: Best visited in combination with the neighbouring Musti and El Krib; a modest site best located using coordinates.
thacia.d: A city from Roman Africa and a former bishopric, the ruins of which are situated near El Krib (Siliana).

thaenae (thyna).a: A Roman city south of Sfax, at the far end of the Fossa Regia: remains of thermal baths, basilicas and mosaics.
thaenae (thyna).c: A sprawling site with little shade, right by the sea: make sure you bring water and wear sturdy shoes.
thaenae (thyna).d: A Roman city south of Sfax, at the far end of the Fossa Regia, featuring thermal baths, basilicas and mosaics.

thala (ville).a: A high-altitude town (~1,017 m) that has retained its ancient name, one of the highest and coldest in Tunisia.
thala (ville).c: Wrap up warm; combine this with a visit to the archaeological site of Thala.
thala (ville).d: A town in the governorate of Kasserine, at an altitude of around 1,017 metres, one of the highest and coldest in Tunisia.

thapsus (ras dimass, bekalta).a: The remains of the Roman harbour and submerged breakwaters; the site of the battle where Caesar defeated the Pompeians in 46 BC.
thapsus (ras dimass, bekalta).c: Scattered coastal site; of mainly historical interest.
thapsus (ras dimass, bekalta).d: Former Carthaginian and later Roman port city at a place called Ras Dimass (Bekalta, Monastir). Punic, Roman and medieval remains, threatened by urbanisation and erosion.

theatre de bulla regia.a: The Roman theatre at the Bulla Regia site, where the tiers of seating and the orchestra are still clearly visible.
theatre de bulla regia.c: Included in the tour of Bulla Regia; well worth a visit whilst exploring the whole site.
theatre de bulla regia.d: The Roman theatre at the archaeological site of Bulla Regia, near Jendouba.

theatre de chemtou (simitthus).a: The Roman theatre of ancient Simitthus, on the banks of the Medjerda.
theatre de chemtou (simitthus).c: Included in the tour of Chemtou; to be explored alongside the quarries and the museum.
theatre de chemtou (simitthus).d: Roman theatre of ancient Simitthus (Chemtou), on the banks of the Medjerda.

theatre de dougga.a: The well-preserved tiers of seating for around 3,500 spectators; the stage and the view over the plain of the Khalled wadi.
theatre de dougga.c: Sit at the top of the tiers to enjoy the panoramic view; still used in summer for performances.
theatre de dougga.d: The Roman Theatre of Thugga, built in the 2nd century, set against the hillside and well-preserved, is still used for performances.
theatre de dougga.h: Site managed by the AMVPPC — open during the day; opening hours vary depending on the season, so please check on site.

thelepte (site archeologique).a: A vast field of ruins (~100 ha) with mosaic-adorned thermal baths, eleven Christian churches and a Byzantine citadel.
thelepte (site archeologique).c: About 5 km north of Feriana; a sprawling, exposed site – take water with you and allow plenty of time for walking.
thelepte (site archeologique).d: A vast site (~100 ha) approximately 5 km north of Feriana (Kasserine). Baths with mosaics, eleven Christian churches and a Byzantine citadel.

thermes d'antonin.a: The imposing substructures by the sea (the vaulted service level that supported the halls), the tall column that gives a sense of the building’s dizzying scale (originally over 30 metres high), the frigidarium and the pools, and the view over the Gulf of Tunis.
thermes d'antonin.c: Combine a visit with the other sites in Carthage (Byrsa and its museum, Roman villas) on the same ticket; come in the morning to enjoy the light and the cool sea air – allow around 45 minutes.
thermes d'antonin.d: Vast public baths built in Carthage during the reign of Antoninus Pius, on the seafront. Among the largest baths in the Roman world.
thermes d'antonin.h: Site managed by the AMVPPC — open during the day; opening hours vary by season, so check on site.

thermes d'oudhna (uthina).a: The grand public baths of the Roman colony of Uthina, with their rooms and substructures, in the archaeological area of Oudhna.
thermes d'oudhna (uthina).c: Worth seeing as part of a general tour of the Oudhna site.
thermes d'oudhna (uthina).d: The great public baths of the Roman colony of Uthina (Oudhna), south of Tunis.

thermes de julia memmia (bulla regia).a: The large public baths dating from the 2nd century, among the most imposing monuments in Bulla Regia thanks to their well-preserved walls and vaults.
thermes de julia memmia (bulla regia).c: A highlight of the tour of Bulla Regia; look up at the tall structures still standing.
thermes de julia memmia (bulla regia).d: The Great Public Baths of Bulla Regia (2nd century), among the city’s most imposing monuments.

thermes romains de djebel oust.a: The thermal baths surrounding the hot spring, with their mosaics still in place, and the early Christian structures that succeeded them.
thermes romains de djebel oust.c: A specialist site with few visitors; check for access details; best combined with a visit to Zaghouan.
thermes romains de djebel oust.d: A Roman thermal bath complex built around a hot spring at Djebel Oust (mosaics), later converted into an early Christian complex.

thibaris (thibar).a: The remains of the basilica and amphitheatre of the ancient Roman colony, set in a rural landscape.
thibaris (thibar).c: A small, modest site: a brief stop is sufficient, to be combined with the other ancient cities in the Medjerda Valley.
thibaris (thibar).d: An ancient Roman city built on the site of a colony of Marius’s veterans, which later became a municipality. Basilica and amphitheatre; a Christian bishopric is attested from 256.

thignica (ain tounga).a: The clearly visible Byzantine fortress overlooking the site, as well as the remains of temples, thermal baths and Roman dwellings in the Medjerda Valley.
thignica (ain tounga).c: A quick stop on the road from Testour to Dougga; walking shoes are recommended to approach the fortress.
thignica (ain tounga).d: Ancient city in the Medjerda Valley, near Testour and Dougga. Notable remains of a Byzantine fortress, temples, thermal baths and dwellings.

thuburbo majus.a: The Capitol standing on its podium; the paved forum; the winter and summer baths and the Petronii gymnasium.
thuburbo majus.c: A peaceful, undulating site, best visited in combination with the nearby Temple of the Waters of Zaghouan.
thuburbo majus.d: A prosperous Roman city in the 2nd–3rd centuries, featuring a forum, a Capitol, temples and thermal baths (winter and summer) which are still visible.
thuburbo majus.h: Site managed by the AMVPPC — open during the day; opening hours vary according to the season, so please check on site.

thuburnica.a: The Roman bridge, thought to date from the time of Trajan, is still standing, along with various scattered remains of the ancient city in the countryside.
thuburnica.c: A small, remote rural site: a car and sturdy footwear are essential; best combined with a visit to nearby Chemtou.
thuburnica.d: A Roman city in north-western Tunisia, featuring a Roman bridge attributed to the time of Trajan and various other remains.

thunusuda (sidi-meskin).a: The scattered remains of this ancient city in the Medjerda Valley, a former episcopal see, between Chemtou and Bulla Regia.
thunusuda (sidi-meskin).c: A modest and largely undeveloped site near Bou Salem: a short stop, best combined with the major neighbouring sites.
thunusuda (sidi-meskin).d: A city of Africa Proconsularis in the Medjerda Valley, between Chemtou and Bulla Regia, near Bou Salem. An ancient episcopal see.

tisavar (ksar rhilane).a: Roman fort (centenarium) on the Limes, isolated on the edge of the desert near Ksar Ghilane.
tisavar (ksar rhilane).c: Access via a Saharan track: 4x4 and a guide recommended; take water with you.
tisavar (ksar rhilane).d: Roman fort (centenarium) of the Limes Tripolitanus, isolated on the edge of the desert near Ksar Ghilane.
tisavar (ksar rhilane).h: Site managed by the AMVPPC — open during the day; opening hours vary according to the season, so please check on site.

tophet de carthage.a: Hundreds of votive stelae to Baal Hammon and Tanit; funerary urns lined up in the open-air enclosure.
tophet de carthage.c: A short visit; arrive early before the heat sets in and combine it with a visit to the adjacent Punic ports.
tophet de carthage.d: The open-air sanctuary of Punic Carthage (the Tophet of Salammbo), where funerary urns and votive stelae dedicated to Baal Hammon and Tanit were placed.
tophet de carthage.h: Site managed by the AMVPPC — open during the day; opening hours vary according to the season, so please check on site.

touiref.a: A village in the north of Kef, near the ruins of Masculula.
touiref.c: A possible starting point for a trip to the ancient site of Masculula.
touiref.d: A town in the north of the Kef governorate.

toujane.a: A Berber village clinging to the slopes of the Matmata mountains, renowned for its weaving and terraced fields.
toujane.c: The scenic route from Matmata is superb: drive slowly to enjoy the views.
toujane.d: A Berber mountain village clinging to the slopes of the Matmata mountains, renowned for its weaving and terraced landscape.

toukabeur (thuccabor).a: The hilltop village on the site of ancient Thuccabor, with its Roman ruins and ancient mosque, forming a heritage pairing with Chaouach.
toukabeur (thuccabor).c: Best visited in combination with Chaouach as part of the same excursion; a vehicle is required for the ridge roads.
toukabeur (thuccabor).d: A hilltop village on the site of ancient Thuccabor, with Roman ruins and an ancient mosque. A heritage site alongside Chaouach.

tourbet el bey.a: The décor of faience and marble; the striking contrast between the unassuming alleyway and the opulence of the interior.
tourbet el bey.c: Often overlooked by visitors: a peaceful haven to the south of the medina. Best visited in conjunction with the neighbouring Dar Ben Abdallah.
tourbet el bey.d: The royal necropolis of the Husaynid dynasty, built in the 18th century. Beneath its domes lie beys, princes and ministers. The interior boasts sumptuous décor — polychrome faience, carved marble and chiselled stucco — blending Italian, Andalusian and Ottoman influences. The men’s tombs are topped with a stele bearing a chechia, whilst those of the women remain unadorned.

tourbieres de dar fatma.a: The high-altitude peat bogs of Kroumirie, a rare wetland in Tunisia, within a nature reserve.
tourbieres de dar fatma.c: A sensitive natural site with few facilities: walk with care, ideally with a guide, in spring.
tourbieres de dar fatma.d: Kroumirie High-Altitude Peat Bogs Nature Reserve, a rare wetland in Tunisia. Approximate coordinates.

turris tamalleni (telmine).a: Ancient site at the western end of the Limes: a Roman fort, later a municipality under Hadrian, and the centre of the Nybgenii tribe.
turris tamalleni (telmine).c: Modest open-air ruins: a guide helps to interpret them; bring water and a hat.
turris tamalleni (telmine).d: Ancient site near Telmine, at the western end of the Limes Tripolitanus: a Roman fort which later became a municipality under Hadrian, and the centre of the Nybgenii.

uchi maius (henchir-ed-douames).a: The Arch of Alexander Severus and the Arch of Gordian III, the forum, the thermal baths and the basilica of this Numidian-Roman city near Dougga.
uchi maius (henchir-ed-douames).c: The site is off the main roads: arrange for a guide or a suitable vehicle and combine a visit with Dougga.
uchi maius (henchir-ed-douames).d: A Numidian city that came under Roman control after Jugurtha, and was established as a colony under Severus Alexander. The Arch of Severus Alexander, the Arch of Gordian III, the forum, the thermal baths and the basilica.

uppenna (henchir chigarnia).a: Ancient site north of Enfida with an early Christian basilica, from which the famous epigraphic mosaics in the Enfida Museum originate.
uppenna (henchir chigarnia).c: The site is rather bare; a visit is best combined with a trip to the Enfida Museum.
uppenna (henchir chigarnia).d: Ancient site north of Enfida with an early Christian basilica. Source of the famous epigraphic mosaics in the Enfida Museum.

utique (utica).a: The House of the Waterfall and its mosaics still in situ; the remains of the thermal baths; the small museum displaying Punic sarcophagi and pottery.
utique (utica).c: A quiet, off-the-beaten-track site; combine your visit with a stop at the Utica Museum on site.
utique (utica).d: An ancient Phoenician city, one of the oldest in North Africa, which later became an important Roman city. Remains of houses with mosaics and necropolises. Today it lies approximately 10 km from the sea (due to silting up of the Medjerda delta).
utique (utica).h: Site managed by the AMVPPC — open during the day; opening hours vary according to the season, so check on site.

uzita (henchir makhrba).a: Ancient city of Phoenician origin and episcopal see of Byzacene, yielding mosaics, near the sebkhas of Sidi El Hani and Sahline.
uzita (henchir makhrba).c: A modest and little-known archaeological site; of interest mainly to enthusiasts of antiquity.
uzita (henchir makhrba).d: Ancient city and episcopal see of Byzacene (Henchir el-Makrceba, Monastir), near the sebkhas of Sidi El Hani and Sahline. Of Phoenician origin, featuring mosaics.

vicus maracitanus (ksar toual zammel).a: A two-storey Numidian-Roman mausoleum with a pilaster-flanked façade, situated in the necropolises of this site linked to the question of Zama.
vicus maracitanus (ksar toual zammel).c: Approximately 15 km south-west of Siliana; a rural site to be located using precise coordinates.
vicus maracitanus (ksar toual zammel).d: An ancient site in the governorate of Siliana, approximately 15 km south-west of Siliana, identified as Vicus Maracitanus. A two-storey Numidian-Roman mausoleum with a pilastered façade stands within its necropolises. Linked to the question of the location of Zama.

vieux port de bizerte.a: The historic harbour, lined with old houses and connected to the sea by a channel, is the picturesque heart of the medina and a former pirate base.
vieux port de bizerte.c: A pleasant stroll along the quays in the late afternoon; the starting point for exploring the kasbah and the medina on foot.
vieux port de bizerte.d: The historic port of Bizerte, lined with old houses and connected to the sea by a channel. The heart of the medina, long a base for corsairs and fishing.

villas romaines de carthage (colline de.a: The House of the Aviary with its reconstructed peristyle and mosaics still in situ, the panoramic terraces and the remains of the Odeon on the hill.
villas romaines de carthage (colline de.c: Beautiful view over Carthage and the sea; to be included in the site’s combined ticket.
villas romaines de carthage (colline de.d: Residential area of Roman Carthage on the Odeon Hill, featuring the House of the Aviary with its peristyle and mosaics, and an odeon. Approximate coordinates.

younga (iunca).a: Roman and Byzantine city south of Mahres, characterised by Christian activity from the 5th century onwards.
younga (iunca).c: Extensive, largely undeveloped coastal site: bring water and sturdy footwear.
younga (iunca).d: Ancient Roman and Byzantine city south of Mahres, with Christian activity dating back to the 5th century.

zaafrane.a: Oasis village, gateway to the Grand Erg Oriental and centre of the Adhara nomads.
zaafrane.c: Starting point for excursions into the dunes: 4x4 or camel treks at sunrise/sunset.
zaafrane.d: Oasis village in the governorate of Kebili, gateway to the Grand Erg Oriental and centre of the Adhara nomads.

zaghouan (ville).a: The Ottoman medina with its ancient fountains, the Roman arch, the silhouette of the Djebel in the background and, overlooking it all, the Temple of the Waters.
zaghouan (ville).c: A pleasant, cool high-altitude base from which to explore the Temple of the Waters and the Djebel National Park.
zaghouan (ville).d: A mountain town at the foot of Djebel Zaghouan. A Roman nymphaeum (Temple of the Waters) and an Ottoman medina with ancient fountains.

zama regia (jama).a: The remains of the Numidian city that became a Roman colony, including a temple with numerous sculptures; its location was confirmed by an inscription in 2002.
zama regia (jama).c: A rural site near Jama, with few facilities: make sure you have precise coordinates to find it.
zama regia (jama).d: A Numidian city near Jama, which later became a Roman colony. Its location was confirmed by an inscription in 2002; the site features a temple with numerous sculptures.

zaouia de sidi bou makhlouf.a: The mausoleum of El Kef’s patron saint, with its domes and octagonal minaret, at the foot of the Kasbah’s ramparts.
zaouia de sidi bou makhlouf.c: A short visit, to be followed by a climb up to the nearby Kasbah.
zaouia de sidi bou makhlouf.d: A zaouïa housing the tomb of Sidi Bou Makhlouf, patron saint of El Kef, at the foot of the Kasbah ramparts (from the 17th century), with domes and an octagonal minaret. Approximate coordinates.

zaouia de sidi kassim el jelizi.a: The polychrome ceramic decoration (zellij) covering the zaouïa, the tomb of the saint and faience maker, and the collections of the National Ceramics Museum housed on the site.
zaouia de sidi kassim el jelizi.c: A gem of faience, set slightly apart; ideal for those interested in the decorative arts, a short visit.
zaouia de sidi kassim el jelizi.d: Zaouïa in the Medina of Tunis with its ceramic (zellij) decoration, tomb of the saint and potter Sidi Kassim El Jelizi. Ceramics Museum.

zaouia de sidi sahbi (mosquee du barbier.a: The courtyards and covered galleries adorned with polychrome faience and chiselled stucco; the mausoleum of a companion of the Prophet.
zaouia de sidi sahbi (mosquee du barbier.c: One of the finest examples of ceramic decoration in Tunisia; modest dress required.
zaouia de sidi sahbi (mosquee du barbier.d: A zawiya housing the mausoleum of Abu Zamaa al-Balaoui, a companion of the Prophet known as Sidi Sahbi, the patron saint of Kairouan. Rebuilt in the 17th century (madrasa, minaret, Hispano-Moorish decorations).

zaouia sidi el arbi (ras jebel).a: The zaouïa and mausoleum of Sidi El Arbi at Ras Jebel, a place of local worship.
zaouia sidi el arbi (ras jebel).c: A small place of worship: a brief visit, best combined with a trip to the Andalusian villages along the coast (Raf Raf, Metline).
zaouia sidi el arbi (ras jebel).d: The zaouïa and mausoleum at Ras Jebel, a place of local worship.

zaouia sidi naceur (testour).a: The zaouïa and mausoleum of the saint Sidi Naceur, a testament to Testour’s Andalusian heritage.
zaouia sidi naceur (testour).c: A brief stop to combine with the other Andalusian monuments in Testour.
zaouia sidi naceur (testour).d: The zaouïa and mausoleum of the saint Sidi Naceur in Testour, part of the Andalusian heritage.

zaouia-mosquee sidi boulbaba (gabes).a: A complex dedicated to Sidi Boulbaba, a companion of the Prophet and the patron saint of Gabès, housing the ethnographic museum.
zaouia-mosquee sidi boulbaba (gabes).c: Appropriate attire; combine your visit with a trip to the adjoining ethnographic museum.
zaouia-mosquee sidi boulbaba (gabes).d: The Sidi Boulbaba zaouïa-mosque complex, dedicated to Abu Lubaba al-Ansari, companion of the Prophet and patron saint of Gabès. It houses the Gabès Ethnographic Museum.

zarat.a: A coastal town south of Gabès, with a fishing harbour.
zarat.c: Small-town harbour atmosphere; of mainly local interest.
zarat.d: A coastal town in the governorate of Gabès, south of Gabès, with a fishing harbour.

zarzis (gergis).a: A seaside resort flanked by olive groves, on the site of ancient Gergis.
zarzis (gergis).c: Beaches and coastal relaxation; can be combined with a visit to nearby Djerba.
zarzis (gergis).d: A coastal town in the south-east, a seaside resort fringed by olive groves, on the site of ancient Gergis.

zones humides de la skhira.a: Wetland complex in the south of the Sfax governorate (Chott el Guetayate, the Akarit, Rekhama and Meleh wadis), important for birdlife.
zones humides de la skhira.c: Ornithological interest: binoculars recommended; birdwatching from a distance.
zones humides de la skhira.d: Wetland complex in the south of the Sfax governorate (Chott el Guetayate, Akarit/Rekhama/Meleh wadis), important for birdlife.

zraoua.a: A Berber village perched on a plateau in the Matmata Mountains, partly deserted since the late 1970s.
zraoua.c: Arid mountainous area: bring water and sturdy footwear.
zraoua.d: Berber village perched on a plateau in the Matmata Mountains (Nouvelle Matmata, Gabès). The inhabitants migrated to a village on the plain in the late 1970s.
